title: Expose exact merge-candidate lineage and CI freshness in Cara status
description:
Operator-requested observability gap found during Cacophony native merger operation. `cara status` reported the caravan graph and aggregate health, but the merger still had to call GitHub directly to learn each active PR's exact current base/head, synthetic merge-candidate SHA and parents, auto-merge owner, check-run generation, and whether visible required checks belonged to the current candidate or a stale head/base generation.

Concrete evidence: Cacophony PR #1991 was head `affacaba74132a4642c6aa06021bb8fa5e381097` on main `251d04e9be9742cbf9a9d2cfa0a194601e5a2561`, while its failed workflow selected stale synthetic merge ref `ff68423484b0be2ffe0a2dd70999c8d518c0887b` whose second parent was prior head `329c42e2a22db8146dada382811927e38ee80e50`. Cara status showed a healthy six-member graph but not this generation mismatch.

Extend stable JSON/MCP status and show output for each active member with: provider-updated timestamp; exact base ref/OID; exact head ref/OID; current synthetic merge-candidate SHA/tree/parents when available; native auto-merge enabled/method/actor; required check names and latest check/run IDs with head/candidate association; and an explicit fresh/stale/unknown classification. Bound output and preserve secret-free receipts. Acceptance: a merger can prove current PR identity, candidate lineage, sole auto-merge ownership, and check freshness from Cara alone without `gh pr view`, `gh api commits/refs/pull/.../merge`, or direct check-runs calls.

## Additional operator gap: default-branch movement provenance

The operator asked who, besides Cara/caco-merger, was advancing `main` and invalidating the caravan. Cara status exposed only current default-branch OID `251d04e9...`; answering required an external git-history inspection. Extend the same bounded provider snapshot with recent default-branch movements: commit/merge SHA, timestamp, author/provider actor when available, source PR or Cara operation receipt, and an explicit Cara-owned versus external classification. Include previous observed default OID so an agent can distinguish actual main motion from a stale GitHub synthetic merge-ref race. Acceptance: Cara alone can report which actors advanced main since the prior sync and which active caravan candidates became stale as a result.
creator: helsinki:cacophony:helsinki-cacophony-caco-merger

title: Reject current-main no-op candidates instead of replaying trunk advances onto the caravan tail
description:
Operator-reproduced Cara join bug in `harryaskham/cacophony` on 2026-07-21. Harry was on branch `fix-cara-timeouts` and attempted to join what was an empty/no-op candidate relative to current default branch. Instead of refusing the empty candidate, Cara created PR #2080 and inferred the already-landed default-branch advance as candidate work, rebasing that unrelated release commit onto the active caravan tail.

Exact graph/evidence:

- Active predecessor PR #2079: head `fix-slackiq-nodes` at `c059bf15b65de83aac8053be5a0c57f785e9c6b3`, parent/default fork `80bf4eacae7451390c2c59c369f1221affcb1c87`.
- True GitHub `main` had already advanced from `80bf4eacae` to release commit `d9fad17e1866272e69a50a47bbd018a890ec33a7` (`release: v1.2.1562`). The authoritative annotated tag v1.2.1562 also peels to `d9fad17e`.
- Cara created PR #2080 with base `fix-slackiq-nodes`, head `fix-cara-timeouts`, initially containing `ac701198a85e07d7964298fe181549b0f2724680`.
- `ac701198` has parent `c059bf15`, author `Cacophony Daemon`, committer `Caravan`, and exactly the same release message/patch as already-main commit `d9fad17e`; it is the default-branch release change replayed onto the caravan tail.
- PR #2080 body identifies the unrelated update-helper source (`agent/ms-dev-2/.../update-helper`, source head `e3026e0461`, mode `direct`) even though the provider head branch is Harry's `fix-cara-timeouts`.
- PR #2080 was created at 23:06:39Z. The timeline later records a head force-push at 23:08:19Z and Harry's actual `fix cara timeoutes` commit `21097975f0377f3294eaa3798be6b83e301a7633` only afterwards; current PR files therefore mix the unintended release bump with the intended `.caravan/config.yaml` edit.

This proves the join/rebase delta was derived against the stale caravan/root fork (`80bf4eacae`) rather than the live provider default tip (`d9fad17e`) / candidate's intended patch. As a result, a branch with no intended delta from current main can silently acquire every trunk commit landed since the caravan fork, and Cara can force-update an operator branch with unrelated duplicated commits.

Expected contract:

1. Under the join lock, re-read the live provider default tip and candidate head.
2. Compute candidate intent relative to that live default/fork-point contract, not relative to the active predecessor's old main base.
3. If candidate has no delta from live default, refuse with a typed `empty_diff`/no-op result and do not create/reuse a PR, mutate/force-push its head branch, append membership, or schedule CI.
4. If candidate has one real change X atop newer default M1 while the caravan tail descends from older M0, rebase only X onto the locked tail; never replay M0..M1 as candidate work.

Required regression test graph: create M0 and a caravan tail T from M0; advance default to M1; (a) join candidate C=M1 and assert a typed no-op with zero provider/membership mutations; (b) join C=M1+X and assert the joined result is T+X only, with M1's already-main patch excluded. Also assert an unrelated existing/current operator branch name cannot be selected or force-pushed as the head of another source generation.

## Live automatic-admission no-op blocker — Cacophony PR #2104

After first caravan #2111 merged, operator-prioritized exact-clean #2104 became canonical. Sync source analysis proved its sole source commit 27815c9a6f13fb2618b6c0cae83ac1ab52183022 already landed in current main79a9d38; effective patch is empty, mutated=false. Cara returned join_empty_source_noop with wake_class=retry_tick and left the PR open/priority-labelled, so unchanged retries block all later candidates forever.

Extend this bead acceptance: sync-owned admission must classify exact already-landed source as terminal/advisory retirement, not retry. Under exact ancestry/tree proof, remove queue control priority/skip intent as appropriate, emit a typed already_landed/noop receipt, and continue to later candidates in the same bounded tick or provide an explicit safe PR-close/Caco-return continuation. Never replay main or report success as a new caravan. Cover root/tail admission, squash-equivalent distinct OID, mixed source where only some commits landed, and concurrent main movement.

title: Add idempotent Cara repository initialization for required labels
description:
## Operator expectation

While integrating Cara into Cacophony, Harry asked whether first use correctly initializes a repository by creating the `caravan`, `caravan-evicted`, and `caravan-force` labels.

Current behavior does not initialize them. `cara status` can inventory an unlabelled repository, but mutation paths call `require_labels` and fail before provider mutation with `required_labels_missing`, instructing the operator to create all three labels manually and rerun. There is no `cara init` command.

The Cacophony repository currently has all three labels, verified through GitHub, but they were provisioned externally rather than by Cara first-use initialization.

## Acceptance

- Add an explicit, idempotent first-party initialization surface such as `cara init` (CLI/MCP), or an equally clear reviewed first-use path.
- Create exactly the required labels with documented names, descriptions, and colors:
  - `caravan`
  - `caravan-evicted`
  - `caravan-force`
- Preserve compatible existing labels without mutation; fail closed on incompatible definitions unless an explicit repair option is chosen.
- Return stable receipts distinguishing created, already-present, incompatible, and provider-failed labels.
- `cara status` should report repository initialization readiness and the exact next command when labels are missing.
- `new`, `join`, `renew`, and `rejoin` continue to fail before graph mutation if initialization has not completed.
- Add provider fixtures for empty repo, partial labels, compatible existing labels, incompatible metadata, retry after partial provider failure, and idempotent replay.
- Document whether automatic initialization is ever allowed; avoid hidden label mutation from a read-only `status` call.

Filed from the first Cacophony Cara cutover. This belongs in the Caravan project, not Cacophony.

title: [broken-on-main] Cara repair start segfaults under canonical nix run
description:
## Live failure

After Caravan bd-dbb5bb fixed the hermetic Git identity tests, caco-merger retried the first-party PR #1962 repair path with the newly landed canonical binary.

- Authoritative Caravan daemon checkout was verified clean with local `HEAD == origin/main == 157ebd32f00334a4645b0aac4026eaf707d464d5`.
- `nix run <checkout> -- --version` succeeds and reports Cara 0.0.2.
- Exact `nix run <checkout> -- repair start --pr 1962` terminates with signal/exit 139, zero stdout, and zero stderr.
- One bounded repeat was made only to capture bytes and exit status; it reproduced identically.
- No repair-workspace manifest was created under the Cacophony Git common directory.
- No provider mutation, raw Git fallback, or PR branch update occurred. PR #1962 remains at exact head `05fe82fe` with auto-merge disabled.

This is a distinct runtime blocker after the test/package build fix: the supported repair command now builds but crashes before it can return a typed decision or create durable recovery state.

## Required outcome

- Reproduce the packaged `nix run ... -- repair start` crash in a clean fixture without relying on user/global Git configuration.
- Identify and remove the signal-139 root cause, including any unsafe/FFI, allocator, subprocess, Git-library, or Nix runtime-library mismatch involved. Record a bounded diagnostic/backtrace or equivalent root-cause receipt.
- Add a regression that executes the packaged repair-start binary, not only direct Rust library tests, and proves it never terminates by signal with empty diagnostics.
- On all preflight/provider/config failures, return the stable structured Cara error envelope and nonzero ordinary exit code; never crash.
- Preserve atomicity: either no repair manifest/workspace/provider mutation occurs, or a complete receipt-bound manifest is durably written. Partial crash state must remain detectable and recoverable.
- Prove `nix run <clean current checkout> -- --version` and `nix run ... -- repair --help` succeed, then exercise repair start/status/abort against a deterministic fixture through the same packaged binary.
- Publish a canonical landed SHA/version receipt before caco-merger retries live PR #1962 at exact head `05fe82fe`. No raw Git/worktree workaround is allowed.

Root-cause redirect: nonmutating clean-environment control (`env -i HOME PATH XDG_CONFIG_HOME`) makes the exact packaged binary return a normal typed error instead of SIGSEGV. Existing Cacophony bead `bd-d7d543` already contains the exact mixed-glibc proof: inherited `NIX_LD`, `NIX_LD_LIBRARY_PATH`, and foreign `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` combine glibc 2.40 loader with glibc 2.42 libc and fault in `dlsym` during `std::Thread::new`. It owns `scripts/cara-runtime.sh`, provenance/pin checks, sanitized invocation, PR #2011, and deployment acceptance. No Caravan domain/runtime change is warranted; an exploratory uncommitted Nix wrapper was discarded. Duplicate is cross-project `cacophony:bd-d7d543`.

title: Show exact compatible and conflicting Saloon targets
description:
Live Cacophony PR #2088 is GitHub CONFLICTING/DIRTY and exact `cara check --pr 2088` reports eligible=false, next_action=reject, conflict path scripts/test-release-helpers.sh, yet Saloon shows Ready to Roll because app.js maps every non-draft admission candidate to ready before compatibility preflight. Hooks may later route repair but never silently resolve conflicts.

Project exact per-candidate compatibility against the current default branch and every current Caravan tail into status/web state under deterministic bounds. Saloon rows must show compatible destinations as `Ready (main, PR #T...)` and incompatible destinations as `Conflicting (main, PR #T...)`; mixed candidates show both. If no caravan exists, main still must be evaluated. Unknown, stale, truncated, timed-out, or unevaluated targets are `Unknown/checking`, never Ready. Preserve exact target branch/OID, tail PR/caravan ID, outcome, bounded conflict paths/diagnostic, provider freshness, evaluation completeness, and generation fingerprint in JSON/MCP/web state. Canonical priority/FIFO order remains separate and does not imply compatibility.

Acceptance:
- #2088 fixture: Conflicting (main), not Ready; exact path available in details.
- Candidate conflicting with main but clean after tail #A: Ready (PR #A), Conflicting (main).
- Candidate clean for main and tails #A/#B: Ready (main, PR #A, PR #B).
- Candidate conflicting for every exact target: Conflicting list and mechanical repair continuation.
- Empty fleet evaluates main.
- Target/candidate movement invalidates cached projection; no stale Ready.
- Bounded large fleet/candidate inventory reports truncation/unknown without N×M unbounded Git/provider work.
- Web action fingerprints include reviewed target compatibility so mutation still revalidates fresh facts.
- Tests cover UI labels/order/accessibility, typed schemas, timeout/provider race, and no provider mutation during projection.

title: Reject Cara join when candidate patch already landed on default branch
description:
## Live reproduction

While joining Cacophony PR #2080 (`fix-cara-timeouts`) to an active caravan, Cara physically rebased an already-landed release patch onto caravan tail `fix-slackiq-nodes` and enrolled the result instead of rejecting it as already present on the default branch.

Exact observed generations:

- default branch `main`: `d9fad17e1866272e69a50a47bbd018a890ec33a7` (`release: v1.2.1562`), parent `80bf4eacae7451390c2c59c369f1221affcb1c87`
- caravan tail/base: `c059bf15b65de83aac8053be5a0c57f785e9c6b3`, also parented by `80bf4eacae7451390c2c59c369f1221affcb1c87`
- rewritten PR head: `ac701198a85e07d7964298fe181549b0f2724680`, parented by the caravan tail
- `git patch-id --stable` for both the main commit and rewritten PR commit: `c8c875993b7fed870c2082837caea490559260e2`
- PR #2080 was force-updated to the rewritten head at 23:08:19Z and then labelled `caravan` at 23:08:56Z.

The rewritten PR therefore contains a patch already integrated on exact current `main`. Its diff against the caravan tail is the release patch, while its diff against current main consists only of unrelated caravan-tail drift. The operator described the source PR as empty/already landed before join.

## Gap

`physical_rebase.rs` rejects `commit_count == 0` relative to the candidate's old provider base (`rebase_empty_patch_range`), but does not reject a non-empty candidate range whose stable patch identity/content is already present on the exact default-branch generation. Rebasing that range onto a stale caravan tail resurrects an already-landed change as a new PR commit.

## Required contract

Before a physical join rewrite or enrollment, compare the candidate-only patch range with the exact current default branch and fail closed when every candidate patch is already represented there (stable patch-id and tree/content proof, with ambiguity rejected). Title: Cara empty-diff join replays another reintegration patch onto caller branch

Operator reproduction on 2026-07-21 exposed cross-reintegration patch contamination while joining Cacophony branch `fix-cara-timeouts` into the active Caravan/Cara tail. The intended operator change was `fix cara timeoutes`, but before that commit was added, Cara/Cacophony synthesized daemon-authored commit `ac701198a85e07d7964298fe181549b0f2724680` on `fix-cara-timeouts` with the complete, unrelated update-helper `release: v1.2.1562` patch and release-agent provenance.

- Its first commit is `ac701198`, parent `c059bf15`, authored by Cacophony Daemon at 23:04:11Z. Its title/body were initially `release: v1.2.1562` and copied update-helper identity/head `e3026e0461`, despite the operator working on `fix-cara-timeouts`.

- If the caller's patch against the selected tail is empty, return an explicit empty/no-op/refusal receipt; do not mutate the caller branch and do not create a PR.
- Refuse when receipt owner/head/patch differs from the branch being joined, even if a recent reintegration has a reusable-looking diff or commit message.
- Preserve the caller branch on any ambiguity and surface exact candidate provenance for diagnosis.

Do not mutate or close PR 2080 as part of triage; preserve it as live evidence until the owner chooses repair.

The initiating `fix-cara-timeouts` PR/branch was believed to have no effective diff. The suspected failure mode is therefore earlier than duplicate-patch replay alone: candidate range inference selected the immediately preceding release commit when the intended source branch was empty, then physical rebase replayed that inferred commit onto the caravan tail.

The fix must first prove the intended provider PR's exact base/head range and reject an empty effective source diff without borrowing a predecessor commit. title: Make caravan-force bypass pending required checks through an explicit force path
description:
Operator contract from Harry: `caravan-force` means bypass required checks for a known spurious CI failure and force/admin-squash the exact eligible caravan head. It must not merely arm normal auto-merge or wait indefinitely for the checks being bypassed. Non-bypassable guards remain: exact current head/base, open same-repository PR, no conflict, clean compatibility, no source/security red evidence, clear ownership, no competing lander/overlap, no active hold, and configured/admin force authority.

Live reproduction on Cacophony with Cara 0.0.2: PR #1991 is OPEN at exact head `97d698c0f514148e5baa03ce952ad05afdaf8389`, base/main `251d04e9be9742cbf9a9d2cfa0a194601e5a2561`, labels `[caravan, caravan-force]`, clean compatibility tree `f6457acc09b87f82bac29164f166faa61f0b4b4b`, sole squash auto-merge, no active hold, and `force_merge: true`. A later provider run `29651416115` remained in progress.

`cara sync --all` did not execute force merge. Source contract currently classifies any Expected/Queued/InProgress check as `Waiting` before checking `failed && forced`, so `caravan-force` cannot bypass a pending required check. No `cara force` command exists (`unrecognized subcommand 'force'`).

Implement an explicit audited force path, preferably `cara force --pr <N> --match-head <sha> --reason/evidence ...`, or equivalent sync semantics that distinguish bypassable required-check state from non-bypassable source/security/compatibility guards. It must re-read exact provider state immediately, require configured force policy and ADMIN permission, prove no competing lander/hold, record evidence and rollback, force-squash once with an exact-head guard, remove/consume force intent idempotently, and advance the child safely. Add CLI/JSON/MCP parity and tests for pending required checks, stale/wrong head, conflict, source/security red, active hold, duplicate retry, and successful forced head advancement.

## Operator CLI confirmation — 2026-07-18

Harry reproduced the same bug from the PR #1991 owner checkout before the manual force land. `cara check` reported `eligible (ActiveCaravan)` with every six-member edge clean. `cara sync` returned `already converged — caravans #1991`, reported `CI #1991: Waiting (14 checks, 0 failed runs)`, and ended with `EnableAutoMerge AlreadySatisfied: head squash auto-merge already enabled`. Despite `caravan-force`, Cara performed no force/admin merge. This confirms the defect is the `Waiting` precedence over force intent, not stale/wrong head, conflict, ownership, overlap, or hold rejection.

title: sync --all exceeds bounded client window and strands a dead operation lock
description:
## Helsinki Cacophony canary

Installed `cara 0.0.1` SHA-256 `2c4b26031301d6730c54029eb24abc2765550ebeb406e1794a13ee4fb7b3ee99` successfully created Caravan #2008 and enrolled its configured maximum eight members. A subsequent root-checkout command:

```text
cara --json sync --all
```

exceeded a 180-second bounded client/tool window and was terminated without a JSON receipt. Provider re-read via `cara --json status` was healthy and showed the complete intended chain with exactly one head auto-merge, but `cara lock status` reported:

```json
{"pid":3406790,"operation":"sync_decision_checkout","token":"3406790-1784334101494090487-1","owner_alive":false,"age_secs":198,"stale_after_secs":1800,"stale":false}
```

No Cara process remained alive. This leaves all later mutations blocked for the default 30-minute stale floor after an ordinary client cancellation/timeout, despite affirmative dead-owner proof.

The merger safely recovered only after re-reading provider state and using exact-token first-party recovery with `--stale-after-secs 180 --confirm`; recovery receipt proved owner dead and token verified.

## Acceptance

- Bound `sync --all` provider inventory/decision work below documented command/client ceilings for a 30-PR repository and an eight-member caravan, or stream/return an accepted operation receipt before the ceiling.
- Release the operation lock through cancellation/termination-safe ownership cleanup when the owning process exits; a dead owner must not strand a fresh non-stale lock solely because the client timed out.
- Preserve fail-closed exact-token recovery for genuinely ambiguous/live ownership.
- Add canaries for SIGTERM/client disconnect during `sync_decision_checkout`, dead owner below the default stale age, live owner, PID reuse/token mismatch, and provider mutation indeterminacy.
- On cancellation after possible provider writes, persist enough operation phase/provider receipts that the next `status`/`sync` can prove replay/no-op safely.
- Keep bounded status JSON and stdout/stderr contracts from bd-f7c3bc.

Implementation/live canary checkpoint on rebased e98eff main: sync now owns one absolute budget `min(5*command_timeout,150s)`, shares it across initial/final status and provider runners (normal child cap remains 30s), and avoids a third full discovery by checking out the exact PR snapshot already embedded in a decision. Operation owner files persist compact phase/exact-precondition receipts and provider-indeterminate state. A later acquisition automatically removes only a twice-read exact-token owner whose PID is affirmatively dead, at any age; live/PID-reused/changed-token cases remain fail-closed. Unit canary sends real SIGTERM to a child holding `sync_decision_checkout`, verifies fresh dead checkpoint survives, then exact recovery succeeds below 30m. Read-only live GitHub canary used a clean Caravan clone and local config with no priority labels: pre-status saw fresh dead pid999999, age0, stale=false, auto_recoverable=true, exact decision_checkout checkpoint. `cara --json sync --all` returned success changed=false, zero caravans/provider writes, exact token-verified lock_recovery including checkpoint, timing total=13,620ms (initial status6,160/provider0/final7,378) under deadline150,000ms; post lock status absent. Provider graph remained healthy.

title: Fail closed when a merged Caravan branch name is reused under a child
description:
Current PR identity and provider mutations are bound to PR number plus exact head/base OIDs, but graph edges are derived by matching an active child baseRefName to active PR headRefName. Race: Caravan parent A on branch B merges; child C still targets B; before sync retargets C, an unrelated new PR D reuses branch name B. GitHub moves B, C now resolves against D, and derive() can silently treat D as C parent because active heads_by_branch takes precedence over merged_by_head. Clean compatibility may not reveal the provenance change.

Fail closed on this historical/active branch-name collision rather than silently reparenting. At minimum, when a child base name is exposed by both a retained merged Caravan PR and a different active PR, report a typed branch-reuse/ambiguous-predecessor graph problem with old/new PR numbers and exact OIDs; do not arm/merge/retarget until operator resolves or the old child is safely advanced. Prefer a durable edge identity bound by join receipt/audit (predecessor PR + generation) if needed beyond conservative detection.

Acceptance:
- Parent merged + child still targeting old branch + new active PR reuses name: invalid graph, zero provider mutation.
- Reuse after every old child has been retargeted: allowed as independent PR.
- Multiple historical uses, active duplicate heads, deleted/fork heads, and provider head/base movement remain fail closed.
- Current/open PR lookup still identifies by unique PR number and exact OIDs; explicit safe historical unlabelled --create-pr behavior remains supported.
- Sync midpoint/concurrent race test proves reuse between discovery and mutation hits exact preconditions.
- CLI/JSON/MCP/status expose actionable old/new provenance; docs warn against premature branch reuse.

title: Cara force heads are rejected by auto-merge invariant before force handling
description:
## Live failure

Cacophony PRs #2053 and #2056 were exact one-member caravans with `caravan-force`, clean compatibility to current main, source/Android checks green, and required checks blocked only by runner Public Fast Tests preparation. Both had native auto-merge disabled.

`cara sync` returned `invalid_graph` before any mutation:

`caravan head #2053 must have squash auto-merge enabled`

The call stack validates the complete fleet graph before CI observation and `force_merge_head`, so an externally force-labelled head cannot reach Cara's audited force branch unless auto-merge is already armed. #2053 also blocked a current-branch sync for #2056 because global graph validation failed on the first unrelated invalid caravan.

Attempting to satisfy the invariant externally with `gh pr merge --auto --squash` merged #2053 immediately because branch protection did not hold it, bypassing Cara's audit/permission/compatibility receipt. The operator then authorized an out-of-Cara admin path for exact green/runner-blocked PRs; #2056/#2057 landed only through that fallback.

## Required behavior

- A current exact `caravan-force` head with `force_merge: true` must reach force validation without requiring pre-existing native auto-merge.
- Cara must validate exact head/default compatibility, external force intent, ADMIN permission, CI evidence, competing landers, and one-shot audit comment before mutation.
- It must atomically force-squash or safely arm-and-force without exposing a window in which native auto-merge can land outside Cara.
- Syncing one selected caravan must not be blocked by an unrelated force-labelled caravan's repairable auto-merge invariant; either repair the selected graph deterministically or return a scoped decision.
- Preserve zero-write behavior on head/default/label/permission drift and at most one force attempt per tick.

## Acceptance

Fixtures cover force head with auto-merge off, unrelated invalid caravan plus selected valid force head, branch protection that would merge immediately on auto-arm, stale force labels, and idempotent post-merge replay. Live Cacophony force no longer requires raw `gh --admin` fallback.

title: cara status segfaults on an adopted current-PR worktree
description:
## Reproduction

Installed binary was built from exact Caravan main `e451ed9c02860f9dea408cd68890fdde56c8846a` after bd-f7c3bc and installed as:

```text
~/.cargo/bin/cara --version
cara 0.0.1
sha256 57674ebff36f28fa576d14bb73044ee4981ba88bec899b4071c52c3f5fc1129b
```

The managed Cacophony root checkout now passes `~/.cargo/bin/cara --json status` (schema 1, healthy, 29 PRs).

From the Cacophony merger's first-party adopted PR #2008 worktree:

```text
cd /home/harry/.cacophony/agents/cacophony/helsinki-cacophony-caco-merger/pr-adoptions/pr-2008
~/.cargo/bin/cara --json status
```

Cara crashes deterministically:

```text
Segmentation fault (core dumped)
exit=139
stdout_bytes=0
stderr_bytes=0
```

Worktree context:

- branch: `agent/pocket4/cacophony/pocket4-cacophony-caco-android-po4-0-pr-g2765f0b235b020fef1b794ef6ebe2cd829c49ce5`
- PR: #2008
- current local/published head: `971386cf4ee1453e7af53d299c823ae888d7e505`
- the branch was adopted through first-party `caco pr adopt`, merged current main, resolved one SPEC conflict, committed, and pushed non-force to the same PR;
- git status is clean.

This blocks `cara check/new/join/sync` formation from the actual PR checkout. Caco-merger must not attempt `cara sync` after a crashing status and remains on its existing audited native path for this PR.

## Acceptance

- Reproduce with a current PR branch whose local/published head contains a merge commit and whose branch name is a Cacophony immutable generation ref.
- Eliminate all panic/abort/unsafe crash paths: every current-PR resolution failure must return a structured JSON error/decision envelope and nonzero normal exit, never SIGSEGV.
- Add deterministic tests for: root checkout with no current PR; ordinary current PR branch; Cacophony generation branch; adopted PR worktree; merge-commit head; stale metadata source head versus newer published head.
- Preserve stdout/stderr separation and large JSON handling from bd-f7c3bc.
- Prove `cara --json status`, `cara --json check`, and the preflight for `cara new/join/sync` are safe from the adopted PR #2008 worktree shape.
- Return an installed-path Helsinki canary request with exact fixed Caravan SHA/version/receipt.

## Regression after operator updater — root status and sync also crash

The operator updater replaced the previously passing installed binary with another `cara 0.0.1` binary:

- current installed SHA-256: `0e88ba61fcb6df4aaf95b609d714d8caae9942be4a0cfcccabb4912e4e59f813`;
- daemon Caravan checkout still reports `e451ed9c02860f9dea408cd68890fdde56c8846a`;
- all three required GitHub labels are present with correct metadata.

From the managed **Cacophony root checkout** (not the adopted worktree), both operator-requested commands now deterministically SIGSEGV:

```text
~/.cargo/bin/cara --json status
exit=139 stdout_bytes=0 stderr_bytes=0

~/.cargo/bin/cara --json sync --all
exit=139 stdout_bytes=0 stderr_bytes=0
```

This broadens the blocker: the crash is no longer limited to current-PR/adopted-worktree resolution. `sync --all` can crash before producing any receipt or decision envelope even with repository labels initialized. No PR mutation was observed; caco-merger stopped immediately.

Acceptance must now include root-checkout installed-binary status and sync-all canaries in addition to adopted-PR coverage, and identify why the operator-installed build hash regressed while the earlier exact-e451 build (`57674e...`) passed root status.

Diagnosis complete; no Caravan status/domain patch. Canonical Helsinki job tj-cc939cc0 proves installed SHA 2c4b2603 (fresh ambient cargo build, glibc 2.42 coherent) returns healthy 30-PR status when `NIX_LD` and `NIX_LD_LIBRARY_PATH` are unset, and SIGSEGVs with inherited managed runtime variables. Preserved core PID 3112435 NT_FILE proves loader/libc mismatch: glibc 2.40 loader plus glibc 2.42 libc; crash is dlsym inside std::Thread::new before a structured status result is possible. Independent matrix: installed/fresh ambient SHA 2c4b passes root and adopted PR #2008; devshell SHA 57daaa and Nix package SHA be2931 use glibc 2.40 and pass clean but deterministically exit139 on both shapes under foreign 2.42 library injection. Cacophony P1 bd-d7d543 owns invocation sanitization and deployment bd-0b9bec depends on it. Accidental duplicate bd-b93947 was marked duplicate. This bead should close redirected; the acceptance demand for a Caravan panic fix is inapplicable because failure occurs in the dynamic loader/runtime environment.

## Current-checkout fallback also SIGSEGVs

Direct operator recovery instructed caco-merger to use `nix run ~/.cacophony/daemon/checkouts/caravan -- <args>` while the installed binary is stale. On Caravan source checkout exact clean head `10db52bcc3415d480a42a7729ecb29691f8fa01b` (`cara 0.0.1`), from the clean first-party PR2012 worktree:

```text
nix run /home/harry/.cacophony/daemon/checkouts/caravan -- check --json
exit=139
stdout_bytes=0
stderr_bytes=0
```

The same current checkout returns `cara 0.0.1` for `--version`, so Nix evaluation/build succeeds and the crash occurs in Cara's PR/current-worktree check path. A prior global-form invocation (`-- --json check`) also produced no usable output. No provider mutation followed: caco-merger failed closed and used its audited exact-head manual path only for the independent green P0 PR2012, outside the active PR2008 hold.

Acceptance should canary both argument orders through installed and `nix run <checkout>` paths and require a structured success/error envelope rather than zero-output exit or SIGSEGV.

### Root-cause clarification

This fallback observation does **not** overturn the closed loader-environment diagnosis above. The managed merger runtime inherited the same foreign `NIX_LD` / `NIX_LD_LIBRARY_PATH` class; wrapping Cara in `nix run` does not sanitize those variables before the produced binary starts. Treat the zero-output SIGSEGV as additional invocation-sanitization evidence for Cacophony `bd-d7d543`, not as a new Caravan domain/status defect. A valid fallback canary must explicitly unset the foreign loader variables before invocation.

title: Cara join must reject or sync stale tail before replaying source commits
description:
## Live reproduction

Operator joined Cacophony branch `fix-cara-timeouts` to stale caravan tail/root PR #2079 (`fix-slackiq-nodes`). Cara produced child PR #2080:

- PR: https://github.com/harryaskham/cacophony/pull/2080
- Base/tail: `fix-slackiq-nodes` at `c059bf15b65de83aac8053be5a0c57f785e9c6b3` (PR #2079)
- Head: `fix-cara-timeouts` at `21097975f0377f3294eaa3798be6b83e301a7633`
- Label: `caravan`
- Head is diverged from true main: ahead 3, behind 1.

PR #2080 contains two commits:

1. `ac701198a85e07d7964298fe181549b0f2724680` — `release: v1.2.1562`, rebased onto stale tail `c059bf15`.
2. `21097975f0377f3294eaa3798be6b83e301a7633` — the operator's actual `fix cara timeoutes` commit.

True main already contains the release as distinct commit `d9fad17e1866272e69a50a47bbd018a890ec33a7`, parented on main `80bf4eac`, with tree `b54319dc`. Cara replayed that already-main release delta into the child because the selected tail was stale. Consequently PR #2080 includes unrelated `CHANGELOG.md`, `Cargo.toml`, and `Cargo.lock` release changes alongside the intended `.caravan/config.yaml` change. Initial PR title/body also came from the replayed release/update-helper commit rather than the unique source commit; the operator subsequently corrected the metadata manually.

Provider events show force-pushes as the branch was materialized. Preserve PR #2080 and branch/event evidence until diagnosis is complete.

## Expected behavior

Before any rewrite, push, PR creation/update, or enrollment, Cara join must prove the selected caravan root/tail is current with the configured base or otherwise has a safe, explicit sync plan. Joining a branch based on newer main to a stale tail must never silently absorb missing-main commits into the child.

Cara must either:

- transactionally sync/rebase the caravan root/tail to current main and then replay only the source branch's unique commits/patch; or
- fail closed with an exact stale-root decision before provider mutation.

Join planning/apply must receipt-bind source repo/branch/head/parent/tree/patch identity, selected caravan/root/tail heads, configured base head, and expected resulting tree. Apply must revalidate all identities and verify the published child contains exactly the unique source patch. PR title/body provenance must come from the intended source commit/operator metadata, never an absorbed main/release commit.

## Regression fixtures

- A source branch based on newer main joining a stale one-PR caravan tail: assert no missing-main commit is replayed into the child.
- Root-current-main invariant drift between preview/apply: fail before push/PR/label mutation.
- Unique source commit plus unrelated release commit already on main: resulting child contains only the unique source patch and uses its title/body provenance.
- Empty unique source patch after subtracting current-main ancestry: return an explicit no-op and perform zero provider mutations.

## Safety

Do not merge PR #2080 in its current form: it duplicates main's release delta and is based on stale non-main ancestry. Do not close, retarget, join again, or otherwise mutate it while preserving the reproduction evidence.

## Canonical Cara 0.0.6 graph and audit evidence

Read-only `cara status --json` with released 0.0.6 confirms:

- active caravan id/root `2079`, members `[2079, 2080]`;
- configured default branch observation `main@d9fad17e1866272e69a50a47bbd018a890ec33a7`;
- PR2079 root `main@80bf4eac -> fix-slackiq-nodes@c059bf15`, auto-merge armed;
- PR2080 child `fix-slackiq-nodes@c059bf15 -> fix-cara-timeouts@21097975`, auto-merge disabled;
- PR2080 synthetic merge/tree `0bd617a166018d3f2c9b949fa67e9cbd746ecc01` / `4413f2fa0dc545e8df41671b8cad6a72a2d7a0ac`;
- compatibility reports both stale-root-to-current-main and child-to-tail as mechanically clean, demonstrating that clean mergeability alone failed to enforce root-current-main ancestry/provenance.

The same released binary's `cara log --pr 2080 --limit 100 --json` returns zero matching records even though provider history records the branch force-push and caravan label. Therefore no durable operation receipt is discoverable from the canonical journal for this mutation. The fix must also guarantee a durable preview/apply operation receipt for join attempts, including no-op/refusal outcomes and every provider mutation identity, so this class of provenance failure is auditable without reconstructing it from GitHub events.

## Merged duplicate: bd-0fe6ad

Title: Reject Cara join when candidate patch already landed on default branch

## Live reproduction

While joining Cacophony PR #2080 (`fix-cara-timeouts`) to an active caravan, Cara physically rebased an already-landed release patch onto caravan tail `fix-slackiq-nodes` and enrolled the result instead of rejecting it as already present on the default branch.

Exact observed generations:

- default branch `main`: `d9fad17e1866272e69a50a47bbd018a890ec33a7` (`release: v1.2.1562`), parent `80bf4eacae7451390c2c59c369f1221affcb1c87`
- caravan tail/base: `c059bf15b65de83aac8053be5a0c57f785e9c6b3`, also parented by `80bf4eacae7451390c2c59c369f1221affcb1c87`
- rewritten PR head: `ac701198a85e07d7964298fe181549b0f2724680`, parented by the caravan tail
- `git patch-id --stable` for both the main commit and rewritten PR commit: `c8c875993b7fed870c2082837caea490559260e2`
- PR #2080 was force-updated to the rewritten head at 23:08:19Z and then labelled `caravan` at 23:08:56Z.

The rewritten PR therefore contains a patch already integrated on exact current `main`. Its diff against the caravan tail is the release patch, while its diff against current main consists only of unrelated caravan-tail drift. The operator described the source PR as empty/already landed before join.

## Gap

`physical_rebase.rs` rejects `commit_count == 0` relative to the candidate's old provider base (`rebase_empty_patch_range`), but does not reject a non-empty candidate range whose stable patch identity/content is already present on the exact default-branch generation. Rebasing that range onto a stale caravan tail resurrects an already-landed change as a new PR commit.

## Required contract

Before a physical join rewrite or enrollment, compare the candidate-only patch range with the exact current default branch and fail closed when every candidate patch is already represented there (stable patch-id and tree/content proof, with ambiguity rejected). Return a typed `already_landed`/empty-effective-diff decision and do not rewrite the head, retarget, label, or enroll the PR.

Add a fixture for sibling histories from one merge base where branch A's patch has already landed on default and joining branch A onto branch B's caravan tail would otherwise replay that patch. Preserve ordinary joining when the candidate has genuinely new effective content.

## Merged duplicate: bd-915573

Title: Cara empty-diff join replays another reintegration patch onto caller branch

Operator reproduction on 2026-07-21 exposed cross-reintegration patch contamination while joining Cacophony branch `fix-cara-timeouts` into the active Caravan/Cara tail. The intended operator change was `fix cara timeoutes`, but before that commit was added, Cara/Cacophony synthesized daemon-authored commit `ac701198a85e07d7964298fe181549b0f2724680` on `fix-cara-timeouts` with the complete, unrelated update-helper `release: v1.2.1562` patch and release-agent provenance.

Exact evidence:

- True GitHub `main` independently and correctly contains release commit `d9fad17e1866272e69a50a47bbd018a890ec33a7`, parent `80bf4eacae7451390c2c59c369f1221affcb1c87`; annotated tag `v1.2.1562` peels to it.
- The active Cara tail/base branch `fix-slackiq-nodes` is `c059bf15b65de83aac8053be5a0c57f785e9c6b3`, also parented by `80bf4eac` and carrying the separate `fix ms agent scope` patch.
- Cara-created/reused PR https://github.com/harryaskham/cacophony/pull/2080 targets `fix-slackiq-nodes` from `fix-cara-timeouts`.
- Its first commit is `ac701198`, parent `c059bf15`, authored by Cacophony Daemon at 23:04:11Z. Its title/body were initially `release: v1.2.1562` and copied update-helper identity/head `e3026e0461`, despite the operator working on `fix-cara-timeouts`.
- `ac701198` contains only the unrelated release metadata patch (`Cargo.toml`, twenty workspace entries in `Cargo.lock`, and `CHANGELOG.md`). It is a duplicate replay of the patch already landed on true main as `d9fad17e`.
- The operator's intended `fix cara timeoutes` commit `21097975f0377f3294eaa3798be6b83e301a7633` was subsequently added on top of the contaminated release commit; live PR 2080 therefore now contains both `.caravan/config.yaml` and the unrelated release patch.

The operator reports Cara first observed an empty diff while he was on `fix-cara-timeouts`, then created PR 2080 and inferred/replayed the diff from main to the Caravan tail. An empty caller patch must never fall back to another agent's most recent reintegration patch, global generation, main-to-tail delta, or stale receipt.

Required behavior:

- Bind join materialization to the exact caller owner, source branch/head, expected base/tail, and patch identity receipt.
- If the caller's patch against the selected tail is empty, return an explicit empty/no-op/refusal receipt; do not mutate the caller branch and do not create a PR.
- Refuse when receipt owner/head/patch differs from the branch being joined, even if a recent reintegration has a reusable-looking diff or commit message.
- Preserve the caller branch on any ambiguity and surface exact candidate provenance for diagnosis.
- Add a regression test with two concurrent patches: release patch A lands on main while operator branch B joins an active tail with an initially empty diff; B must never receive A.

Do not mutate or close PR 2080 as part of triage; preserve it as live evidence until the owner chooses repair.

## Operator clarification

The initiating `fix-cara-timeouts` PR/branch was believed to have no effective diff. The suspected failure mode is therefore earlier than duplicate-patch replay alone: candidate range inference selected the immediately preceding release commit when the intended source branch was empty, then physical rebase replayed that inferred commit onto the caravan tail.

The fix must first prove the intended provider PR's exact base/head range and reject an empty effective source diff without borrowing a predecessor commit. The already-landed-on-default check remains a necessary independent backstop, because the inferred release commit was already represented on current `main`.

Duplicate investigation signal merged from bd-6f3cc3: live canary independently identified the same stale-root physical-rebase shape and adds explicit empty/no-unique-change PR refusal plus already-main patch-equivalence/drop acceptance. Canonical bd-35e822 remains the sole P0 under MSM0; do not implement separately.

## Post-reproduction provider repair

Later provider topology was manually repaired without closing the bug:

- PR2079/root was force-updated to `570e26ea`, parented on release main `d9fad17e`; root squash auto-merge is armed.
- PR2080/child was updated to `829e768b`, parent `570e26ea`, containing only the intended timeout commit/diff.
- The absorbed `ac701198` release delta is no longer present in the live child diff.

This repairs the live unsafe topology but does not erase the reproduced Cara defect. Preserve the original force-push/label event history, exact old heads/trees, zero-record `cara log` result, and regression requirements above. The fix must prevent the initial stale-tail absorption and provide durable operation receipts; a later manual topology correction is not proof of correct join behavior.

## Subsequent root movement clarification

A later read after the initial repair observed PR2079 head advanced again from `570e26ea` to `889dfe2779c72f39306ce5e43a364d17c424bb4a`, a merge commit `Merge branch 'main' into fix-slackiq-nodes` with parents `570e26ea` and `6764c4c2`. PR2080 remains at intended-only commit `829e768b`, parent `570e26ea`, while its provider base branch now resolves to PR2079 head `889dfe27`. This later movement does not change the original defect or evidence; it further demonstrates why join/apply receipts must bind exact root/tail/base heads and fail or explicitly resync on drift rather than relying on branch names.

## Descendant invalidation gap after root movement

Canonical `caco agent merge-queue list` / Cara projection later reported `healthy=true` with both candidates fresh after the root branch moved:

- PR2079/root head `889dfe27` is a merge of prior repaired root `570e26ea` plus current main `6764c4c2`.
- PR2080/child remains head `829e768b`, parent/provider-base OID `570e26ea`; its synthetic merge still records parents `[570e26ea, 829e768b]`.
- `compare 889dfe27...829e768b` is diverged; the child is behind the live root by two commits and their merge base is historical root `570e26ea`.
- Despite that branch-name/base-OID mismatch, projection marks PR2080 `stale_base=false`, `stale_head=false`, and a merge candidate.

Acceptance must enforce descendant invalidation/cascade: whenever a caravan root or intermediate member advances, Cara must transactionally cascade/rebase every descendant to the new exact parent, or mark the caravan invalid/paused before any merge candidate can proceed. Status and merge-queue projection must compare each child's recorded provider base OID with the live parent branch head and must never report healthy/fresh/mergeable from a historical base OID after that branch moved. Add fixtures for root force-update and root merge-update with an unchanged child, including drift between discovery and apply.

## Root-advance false-healthy evidence (2026-07-22)

After the repaired root PR #2079 advanced again to `889dfe27`, child PR #2080 remained based on prior root `570e26ea` with head `829e768b`. Read-only ancestry comparison reports diverged and child two commits behind root, while released Cara's canonical projection still reports `healthy=true`.

Acceptance must therefore cover root advancement after enrollment: descendants must be transactionally rebased/cascaded with durable receipts, or canonical status must fail closed with exact root/child ancestry evidence. A diverged descendant must never remain false-healthy. PRs were left untouched and PR #2078 remains held.

## Eventual descendant-cascade recovery receipt

Provider topology was subsequently corrected again:

- PR2080 head `77199f2597` now targets live root/base OID `889dfe2779`.
- `compare 889dfe2779...77199f2597` reports ahead 1, behind 0.

title: Resolve Git repository root before config discovery and init
description:
Operator reproduction: invoking Cara from a nested directory inside a Git repository reports the repository as uninitialized and then attempts to create `.caravan/` in that nested working directory. Cara currently binds `AppContext.repository_path` and the default `.caravan/config.yaml` to ambient cwd instead of the canonical worktree root.

Resolve the exact repository/worktree root before default config discovery and every Git/GitHub/domain operation (for example, a bounded `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` contract). Default `.caravan/config.yaml`, common Git metadata, operation locks, repairs, status cache identity, dashboard repository IDs, and init writes must consistently use that root. Explicit `--config PATH` remains explicit: define whether relative overrides resolve from invocation cwd or canonical root, preserve the documented contract, and reject symlink/path escape where existing safety requires it.

Acceptance:
- From root and multiple nested subdirectories, `cara status`, `init`, `sync`, navigation, lock, log, web/action context, and JSON/MCP resolve one identical repository/config identity.
- Nested `cara init` creates only `<root>/.caravan/config.yaml`, never `<cwd>/.caravan`.
- Outside Git returns a typed repository-not-found/config continuation and writes nothing.
- Linked worktrees resolve their own worktree root while shared common-Git state remains common where intended.
- Bare repository, symlinked cwd/config, relative and absolute explicit config overrides, `-C`/environment edge cases, and paths containing spaces are covered.
- Root discovery is bounded, noninteractive, secret-free, and occurs before mutation.
- Focused fixtures, CLI/JSON/MCP parity, strict Clippy/fmt, full configured tests, docs/help.

title: Bind caravan-force intent to the exact head generation
description:
Architecture review found one important force-generation gap for deterministic join/sync.

Existing protections are good: membership join removes caravan-force rather than adding/carrying it as a control label; force executes only for a non-successful explicitly labelled head; graph/compatibility and physical-rebase preflight happen first; force re-verifies exact default OID, open/non-draft state, label presence, ADMIN, durable audit comment, non-head auto-merge disable, and exact provider precondition. Routine pr_cara_join must expose no force input and its receipt should prove force absent/removed.

Gap: with rebase_on_join=true, sync physically rewrites a head, rediscovers it, and then evaluates CI in the same tick. An old caravan-force label survives the head-SHA rewrite. Checks on the new generation are initially empty, so the old label can immediately force-merge the newly rewritten generation even if operator intent was attached to the prior SHA. The existing passing-with-stale-force test does not cover this rewrite transition. This weakens stale-head/operator-only semantics.

Required contract: bind force intent to an exact observed head generation (durable comment/marker or equivalent). Any Cara-owned head rewrite must consume/remove or invalidate pre-rewrite force intent; force after rewrite requires a fresh operator action on the new SHA. Add tests for forced-old-generation + physical rebuild + empty checks, stale force label during pr_cara_join, and explicit re-application on the new generation. Keep force absent from healthy sync/join receipts except an explicit invalidation/removal step.

Implementation landed true main at 35c08e6 (reintegration attempt r3jo86y5v9h80nf2-20260719T101948.863Z-26c489eb). Sync removes/audits old-generation caravan-force only after the complete global physical write barrier; membership now prepare_candidate first, then invalidates/audits stale force, then apply_prepared, so planning conflicts consume no intent. Already-satisfied exact generations preserve intent; rewritten generations require a fresh label. Composed with atomic join 780ac5d JoinReceipt. Focused atomic join/force/reapplication tests and strict all-target Clippy passed; prior full suite passed before the one-commit atomic-join rebase. Lifecycle finalization is blocked only by Caco invoking a nonexistent claude-plugin before_complete hook for this Pi worker despite refresh/reload; controller repair requested. Do not manually close; retry caco agent complete after hook resolution.

title: Add optional cumulative rebase mode for physically chained caravans
description:
Operator-directed design/implementation lane. Add strict repository config `rebase_on_join: false` (safe default). When true, Caravan represents a chain both in GitHub PR bases and in Git ancestry so head A is based on exact default, joining B contains only B's patch rebased onto exact A, joining C is rebased onto exact B, and CI on each member validates cumulative A, A+B, A+B+C content.

This mode is explicit history rewriting, not the current virtual compatibility-only contract. Implement with isolated temporary worktrees, exact remote OID fetches, no caller-worktree mutation, full conflict simulation before the first provider write, same-repository/owned-branch and push-permission preflight, and exact `git push --force-with-lease=refs/heads/<branch>:<old-oid>`. Rediscover after every push/base mutation and return old/new head OIDs plus provider receipts. Never force a branch that moved or whose patch range is ambiguous/nonlinear unless a documented safe merge-preserving strategy exists.

Membership: `new` rebases the candidate-only series onto the exact current default; `join`/`rejoin` rebase candidate-only commits from its exact old base/merge-base onto the selected parent before setting the GitHub base. Sync must detect parent OID movement and cascade child-only rebases head→tail under exact leases. Eviction of B from A→B→C must preflight and perform `C --onto A B` (and cascade later descendants) so B content is actually dropped; falling back to the old base while retaining B's patch is not a successful eviction. Split at B must transplant B-only commits onto main and cascade descendants. Any conflict or ambiguous range is a typed resumable decision with zero speculative push.

Preserve current `rebase_on_join=false` behavior and SPEC compatibility. Add interruption/replay, stale lease, merge commit, signed commit, parent update, cascading descendants, evict middle/head/tail, split, conflict, and partial provider failure tests. Live-prove using clearly named disposable PRs on harryaskham/caravan only; do not use Cacophony fixtures. Verify CI trees are cumulative and attach exact tree/OID receipts.

Important limitation to document/test: because current heads squash-merge, retargeting B after A lands can still change GitHub merge-ref/check identity and trigger provider CI even when cumulative tree content is already proven. This mode improves semantic cumulative testing but must not claim instant no-rerun landing until an ancestry-preserving merge mode or audited exact-tree/check receipt policy is implemented.

CI trigger requirement discovered on live Cacophony chain: PR #1991 targets main and has CI; rebased child #1972 targets #1991's `agent/...` branch and has no checks because `.github/workflows/ci.yml` filters `pull_request.branches: [main]`. Rebase mode must preflight/report a compatible workflow trigger contract: CI pull_request must include all possible caravan parent base branches (e.g. remove the main-only filter or include `agent/**`/configured head patterns), and include the `edited` action because changing a PR base emits an edited event; current explicit types omit it. Ensure the post-rebase/base-update event runs on the correct cumulative merge ref. Add fixtures proving A(main), B(agent/A), C(agent/B) each receive the required check. For cumulative semantic proof, use an unfiltered dedicated Caravan stack check/full suite rather than path-skipping required checks. Fail closed with actionable config evidence when required CI cannot trigger on a non-main parent.

CI integration requirement discovered from live Cacophony chain #1991→#1972: GitHub Actions `pull_request.branches` filters the PR base. Repositories whose validation workflows trigger only for `main` will not run CI on downstream members based on another PR branch, so rebase_on_join cannot deliver cumulative validation by itself. Preflight/status must detect absent downstream expected checks and return a typed repository-policy decision with guidance. Documentation/acceptance must require validation workflows to trigger all Caravan base branches (or configured branch patterns) while deployment/release remains main-only. Live Caravan proof must confirm each downstream PR receives its required CI. Checks from a non-main merge ref still do not transfer after retarget/squash; retain the existing limitation.

CI trigger requirement discovered on live Cacophony chain: PR #1991 targets main and has CI; rebased child #1972 targets #1991's `agent/...` branch and has no checks because `.github/workflows/ci.yml` filters `pull_request.branches: [main]`. Rebase mode must preflight/report a compatible workflow trigger contract: CI pull_request must include all possible caravan parent base branches (e.g. remove the main-only filter or include `agent/**`/configured head patterns), and include the `edited` action because changing a PR base emits an edited event; current explicit types omit it. Ensure the post-rebase/base-update event runs on the correct cumulative merge ref. Add fixtures proving A(main), B(agent/A), C(agent/B) each receive the required check. For cumulative semantic proof, use an unfiltered dedicated Caravan stack check/full suite rather than path-skipping required checks. Fail closed with actionable config evidence when required CI cannot trigger on a non-main parent.

Operator-selected CI setup: GitHub Actions cannot filter `on.pull_request.branches` by PR label; that field matches the base branch. Recommended label-gated contract is an unfiltered `pull_request` trigger with types including opened/synchronize/reopened/edited/labeled/unlabeled, then job-level `if` running the stack/full check when base is main OR the PR has the `caravan` label. Thus ordinary main PRs and labelled non-main caravan children run, while unrelated non-main PR jobs skip. Rebase mode must inspect workflow/config and emit a clear project-configuration warning/error (`rebase_ci_trigger_missing`) with remediation when non-main parent bases cannot produce the configured stack check. `cara init/status/check` should surface readiness; sync must not treat an empty child check set as evidence CI passed.

Operator CI contract clarification: GitHub cannot event-filter by PR label and branches have no Caravan tag. Supported pattern is pull_request with no branches filter and types including opened,synchronize,reopened,ready_for_review,edited,labeled,unlabeled; job-level heavy-suite condition checks pull_request label caravan. Labeled covers enrollment and edited covers base retarget. Prefer an always-reported lightweight check plus conditional full suite so missing/skipped evidence is deterministic. Add strict config for expected Caravan check names and a bounded grace period; status/sync must warn/fail closed with code/evidence when an active downstream member has no expected exact-head check/workflow run, without constraining branch names.

title: cara init creates an untracked config that makes sync refuse its own worktree
description:
## Cacophony canary

Sanitized packaged Cara (`cltv-run caravan#cara`, version 0.0.1, store binary `/nix/store/04rswfnfk55a8rpcims63c82zay8v2aq-caravan-0.0.1/bin/cara`) ran from the clean managed Cacophony checkout.

Read-only status correctly reported `repository_not_initialized` for mutations despite all three labels matching. `cara init` then succeeded and returned:

```json
{"ready":true,"config":{"path":".caravan/config.yaml","state":"created"},"labels":[{"name":"caravan","state":"already_present"},{"name":"caravan-evicted","state":"already_present"},{"name":"caravan-force","state":"already_present"}]}
```

The immediately following `cara sync --all` failed before any provider mutation:

```json
{"code":"head_conflict","details":{"checkout":{"error":{"code":"dirty_worktree","details":{"status":"?? .caravan/\n"},"message":"refusing to switch branches because the worktree has tracked or untracked changes"}}}}
```

Cara's own init-created config therefore makes the same repository ineligible for sync's required decision checkout. This deadlocks the documented init→sync recovery path unless the operator manually relocates/ignores the file.

Acceptance:
- `cara init` must place local operational config where its own dirty-worktree guard ignores it safely, or create/verify a reviewed repository-local ignore contract without hiding unrelated files.
- A successful init followed immediately by status/check/sync in an otherwise clean worktree must not fail `dirty_worktree` because of the exact init-owned file.
- Never weaken the dirty-worktree guard for arbitrary `.caravan/` content; recognize only the exact validated config path/inode or use an external state path.
- Add fixtures for newly created config, pre-existing correct config, tracked config, unrelated untracked file beside config, symlink/path escape, alternate `--config` outside the worktree, and branch checkout cleanup.
- Preserve idempotent repository-label/resource receipts and ensure no provider mutation occurs before checkout safety passes.

title: Joining a child onto a stale root absorbs already-main deltas into the child generation
description:
## Live reproduction

During the `pr_cara_join` canary, operator-created root PR #2079 (`fix-slackiq-nodes`, head `c059bf15b65de83aac8053be5a0c57f785e9c6b3`) remained based on stale main `80bf4eacae7451390c2c59c369f1221affcb1c87`. Live main later contained release v1.2.1562 as squash commit `d9fad17e1866272e69a50a47bbd018a890ec33a7` with parent `80bf4eac`.

The local branch used for child PR #2080 (`fix-cara-timeouts`) inherited the release source commit `ac701198a85e07d7964298fe181549b0f2724680`, whose parent is stale-root head `c059bf15`, then added intended timeout commit `21097975f0377f3294eaa3798be6b83e301a7633`. Cara admitted #2080 after stale root #2079 without first converging the root onto current main. Provider state became:

- caravan: `2079 -> 2080`
- #2079 base: `main@80bf4eac` (stale)
- #2080 base: `fix-slackiq-nodes@c059bf15`
- #2080 displayed files include Cargo/CHANGELOG v1.2.1562 even though equivalent release patch is already on live main as `d9fad17e`.

The operator began from what appeared to be an empty `fix-cara-timeouts` branch and expected only the timeout edit. Cara's stale-root admission made the child look as though it invented/absorbed the release delta. This is unsafe/misleading canary topology; PR #2078 is being held until #2079/#2080 are resolved.

## Required behavior

Before appending a child, Cara must converge or refuse a caravan whose root base OID is not live default-branch OID. It must not construct a child generation on a stale root where an already-main patch is represented by a parallel squash/source commit.

## Acceptance

1. Reproduce with stale root `R` from main `M0`, live main `M1` containing squash-equivalent patch `S`, and child source ancestry `R -> S-source -> C`.
2. `join` either atomically advances/rebuilds the root to `M1` before calculating the child, or returns a typed stale-root decision with zero child/provider mutation.
3. After successful convergence, the child provider diff contains only `C`; the duplicate `S-source` patch is dropped as already satisfied.
4. Receipt records old/live main OIDs, root rewrite, duplicate/empty patch disposition, final child base/head/tree, and exact provider mutations.
5. Empty/no-unique-change branches are refused before PR creation/admission instead of allowing inherited predecessor commits to masquerade as the requested change.
6. Add a live/hermetic regression and ensure status/dashboard never describes the absorbed main delta as child-authored work.

title: Add best-effort queue optimisation and auto-admission to sync
description:
## Operator direction — 2026-07-20

Make repeated `cara sync --all` ticks reconcile the fleet and continuously adopt eligible unlabelled PRs, so one Cara loop/controller can eventually drain a long queue without external orchestration scripts.

## Configuration

Add a strict opt-in config surface such as:

```yaml
sync:
  actions:
    join_unlabelled_prs: true
```

Default remains false. Cacophony will opt in.

## Required algorithm

1. Reconcile and validate existing caravans first using normal idempotent sync. A real invalid graph, provider invariant, mechanical/semantic decision, or operator action stops the tick; do not hide it by admitting around it. Waiting CI, held, and healthy states remain structurally valid.
2. If no caravan exists, use the canonical priority/FIFO candidate to form one. Otherwise inspect candidates in configured-priority then immutable-FIFO order and caravans in existing deterministic caravan order.
3. For each candidate, try current tails deterministically. Join to the first exact tail for which candidate/tail and whole-fleet compatibility preflight succeeds. Use the landed atomic remote join receipt, rebase-on-join, and exact-lease contracts; rediscover after every mutation.
4. If no tail works, mark the exact candidate generation with `caravan-join-skipped` plus a durable reason/comment receipt, then consider later candidates in the same tick. This opt-in behavior is an explicit exception to current no-leapfrog automatic admission.
5. A skip must not block manual `new`/`join`/`rejoin`. Bind it to repository, candidate PR/head/base, tested tail generations, default generation, config fingerprint, heuristic version, compatibility reasons, actor, and time. Candidate head/base/config/tail/default/heuristic changes make evidence stale and eligible for automatic retry/removal; unchanged generations are not retried every tick.
6. Bound one tick by wall clock, GitHub API budget, and maximum mutations/candidates. Return exact joins/skips, remaining candidates, and continuation. Retry is idempotent.
7. Expose the heuristic version in status/sync receipts. It is deliberately evolvable; deterministic behavior is required for one version, not permanent optimisation semantics. `priority_fifo_greedy_v1` is sufficient and need not claim a global maximum.
8. `cara loop` and `cara loop --once` consume the same sync behavior. GitHub Actions normally run bounded `--once` ticks from PR/check/workflow/default-branch events plus a schedule, rather than one unbounded hosted job.

Cover empty fleet, one/many caravans, compatible/incompatible candidates, generation-bound skip invalidation, manual override, concurrent tail movement, candidate push, partial crash, API/mutation budget exhaustion, repeated drain, and no admission before existing-fleet convergence. Preserve exact provider rereads, operation lock, and complete audit receipts.

This is the sync-owned best-effort fleet optimiser. Do not add a separate top-level reconcile command unless needed for read-only planning.

title: Separate explicit membership authority from automatic FIFO admission

This is wrong: membership execution already treats every explicit new/join/rejoin as a manual override and consumes advisory skip state. Priority labels are persistent automatic-scheduling metadata, not permission to execute an explicit operator-selected membership action.

Make the contract unambiguous and audit-correct. Explicit `cara join --pr N --tail-pr T` (and explicit new/rejoin equivalents) owns exact mechanical/provider preflight and may select a noncanonical automatic candidate. When selection differs from canonical priority/FIFO, require a non-empty operator reason and record `explicit_manual_override` with selected PR, canonical PR/order evidence, actor/reason, exact generations, and no synthetic priority label. Omission of --priority-label must not be rendered as FIFO when the selected PR is noncanonical. `--priority-label` remains optional only when the operator deliberately wants to mutate persistent automatic-admission rank.

- Supplying configured --priority-label continues to mutate/report rank deliberately, but docs/help say it is not authorization.
- Remote `cara check --pr B` clearly distinguishes `automatic_order_allowed=false` from mechanical eligibility and points to explicit join+reason rather than suggesting priority mutation.

title: Classify failed CI decisions with exact failed-step lineage evidence
description:
Operator-requested Cara information gap. `cara sync --all` correctly returned `ci_failure` for Cacophony PR #1991 and listed failed check names plus rerunnable run ID `29646903145`, but it did not expose why the run failed. The merger had to inspect the GitHub Actions job log directly to discover that the selected ref was stale: expected head `affacaba74132a4642c6aa06021bb8fa5e381097`, selected merge ref `ff68423484b0be2ffe0a2dd70999c8d518c0887b`, parents `[251d04e9be9742cbf9a9d2cfa0a194601e5a2561, 329c42e2a22db8146dada382811927e38ee80e50]`. A blind `cara sync --rerun-failed` would have rerun the same stale event rather than validate the current candidate.

Extend CI decision evidence with bounded structured failure diagnostics: failed job and step names; provider run/job IDs; exact selected ref/SHA; expected and observed base/head; selected-ref parents; current synthetic candidate identity; and a deterministic classification such as stale-merge-ref, retryable-infrastructure, source/test failure, cancelled, or unknown. Prefer first-party structured outputs/check annotations and bounded log extraction; never expose credentials or unbounded logs.

description:

No command may bypass conflicts, stale facts, holds, ownership, graph validity, or permissions. A Cara-owned rewrite invalidates old-generation intent exactly as today.

Add an idempotent first-party revoke path (`cara force revoke --pr N --actor A --reason R`, or an equivalent clear command) that removes only exact current-generation force intent with a durable audit. JSON/MCP/web schemas and receipts must expose before/after labels, PR/head/default generation, observed CI state, actor/reason, mutated flag, and safe continuation. Interactive shorthand may default to the current PR but automation requires explicit identity.

Acceptance:
- Arm exact failed/pending/empty current head and return typed durable receipt; rerun is exact no-op/deduped.
- Typo/unknown label is never treated as intent; help names `caravan-force` exactly.
- Stale head/default, nonmember/evicted/draft/closed PR, incompatible graph, textual conflict, disabled policy, insufficient permission, or comment failure fail closed with zero/partial receipts as appropriate.
- Revoke is exact, audited, idempotent, and never touches unrelated labels.
- Rewrite invalidation and one-shot sync consumption remain generation-bound.
- Full CLI/JSON/MCP/web parity and concurrency tests; docs remove manual-label guidance.

Coordinate with bd-1f3ff4, which fixes force-head graph-validation ordering and is currently owned by msm1; do not overlap that decision-order implementation.

To avoid concurrent web.rs conflicts, bd-885497 no longer owns direct dashboard rendering; the dependent web-controls bead will expose this stable operation alongside the priority command after both domain beads land. Preserve all exact-generation, audit, permission, compatibility, and one-shot acceptance requirements.

Implementation complete at exact rebased generation 26727e7 over main 9ae4d01. Added typed `force_arm`/`force_revoke` domain operations, direct CLI `cara force --pr/--actor/--reason` plus `cara force revoke ...`, JSON/MCP schemas and parity. Arm requires force_merge policy, exact open owned non-draft non-evicted active head, clean head/default compatibility, no graph problem/hold, fresh default/head and ADMIN; then changes only `caravan-force` under exact PR preconditions and posts deterministic generation-bound actor/reason/check audit. title: Add CLI manual decision mode with an interactive shell
description:
## Operator goal

Provide a human-operated way to exercise Cara's full decision/recovery flow without turning production machine hooks into PTY sessions.

## Product surface

Add a CLI-only mode such as:

```text
cara loop --manual [--shell 'zsh -i']
```

or an equivalent explicit `sync --manual` driver. Normal hooks remain noninteractive machine integration.

## Required behavior

- Run the ordinary bounded `sync --all` tick. Healthy/waiting/held/retry outcomes retain normal behavior.
- On `wake_class=external_decision`, persist the complete bounded decision event to a secure temporary/durable file and expose `CARA_DECISION_FILE` plus event/operation/repository/caravan/PR/session continuation variables.
- Checkpoint and release the repository operation lock before launching anything interactive.
- Launch the configured shell with inherited stdin/stdout/stderr and a real controlling TTY, from the exact safe affected checkout or Cara-owned repair workspace when one exists. Refuse non-TTY, JSON, MCP, daemon, or hosted noninteractive invocation rather than degrading silently.
- Do not infer resolution from shell exit alone. Zero exit triggers full provider rediscovery and another sync tick; nonzero exits manual mode while preserving evidence. Exact repair publication still uses `repair continue`, provider head/target checks, and non-force branch rules.
- Bound/recover temporary decision files, redact secrets, preserve a manual-session audit receipt, and handle signals/terminal restoration.
- Document suggested shell helpers for inspecting JSON with `jq`, running tests, invoking authorized repair, and exiting to retry.

Tests should cover inherited TTY and cwd, lock release, decision-file integrity, zero/nonzero exit, signal handling, stale provider movement while shell is open, repair workspace continuation, recursive hook avoidance, and refusal from MCP/noninteractive environments.

Existing hooks already receive JSON on stdin and are synchronously awaited with timeout/blocking policy. Production repair scripts may submit durable agents and poll until exact resolution; this feature is only the human flow-testing/controller surface.

- Its first commit is `ac701198`, parent `c059bf15`, authored by Cacophony Daemon at 23:04:11Z. Its title/body were initially `release: v1.2.1562` and copied update-helper identity/head `e3026e0461`, despite the operator working on `fix-cara-timeouts`.

title: Keep released Cara compatible when config adds sync policy
description:

Current Cacophony main contains a `.caravan/config.yaml` `sync:` policy block. The released Cara 0.0.6 binary fails before any read-only status or sync operation:

`parse .caravan/config.yaml: unknown field sync, expected version/force_merge/rebase_on_join/agent_priority_labels/command_timeout_secs/repair/loop/journal/hooks`

This is another config-before-reader rollout break: existing deployed Cara cannot inspect or operate a repository after the config source advances.

## Required behavior

- Define a rolling-upgrade-safe config contract for newly added policy sections.
- Released readers must either tolerate unknown additive sections safely, or the repository must fail closed before landing config that requires a newer declared minimum Cara version.
- Add an explicit config schema/version or `min_cara_version` capability gate with a typed upgrade message.
- Cacophony's pinned Cara runtime and config must advance atomically; deterministic CI must verify reader/config compatibility before merge.
- Preserve strict rejection for misspelled or security-sensitive keys; do not globally ignore arbitrary unknown fields without an audited extension mechanism.
- Add fixtures proving old-reader/new-config and new-reader/old-config behavior across a rolling deployment.

## Immediate acceptance

Provide a reviewed Cara release/pin that can parse the current `sync` block, then re-run canonical Cacophony status/sync without modifying provider state.
