title: Add audited merge-preserving cumulative rewrite for nonlinear PR ranges
description:
Cacophony #1958 blocks real v0.0.5 queue drain after the external-default lease fix: exact head 6c895352849a4ed7f9ab44df7b068e09944c53da has six merge commits between retained base e1f87cd0f87b8523de08b2c2f7421fe75d672bf1 and head. Cara correctly refuses ordinary linear rebase with `rebase_nonlinear_range`; force/CI labels must not bypass this. Provide an explicit audited strategy for cumulative mode or an equally safe first-party transformation continuation.

If implementing merge preservation, plan the complete exact topology before writes (for example reviewed `--rebase-merges` semantics), retain candidate-only commits and merge relationships, reject external/cross-range parents or ambiguous octopus topology, prove resulting tree/parents/old-base/new-base, retain current-target ancestry and workflow trigger checks, and publish only the candidate head under exact force-with-lease. Multi-member descendants must consume the exact planned rewritten parent. No raw resets or flattening by guess.

Acceptance:
- Fixtures cover main merged into feature repeatedly, internal feature merges, external parent, octopus/ambiguous history, target advance, candidate-head race, and multi-member cumulative chain.
- Supported topology yields deterministic plan plus exact old/new topology/tree receipts and idempotent second tick waiting on fresh CI.
- Unsupported topology remains a zero-write external decision with actionable first-party recovery.
- Live acceptance against retained #1958 from a clean clone succeeds or returns a newly specific unsupported-topology decision; broad drain remains stopped until proven.
- Strict Clippy/fmt, full configured tests, Nix/release contract as appropriate, docs/help.

Live scope update: #1958 was subsequently admin-squash merged through one cluster-authorized, exact-head Cara force operation with rebase_on_join=false and auto-admission=false. The force path did not bypass nonlinear cumulative rewriting; it avoided that mode entirely after exact compatibility/head/base/default revalidation and mutated only the audited comment plus squash merge. Therefore this merge-preserving capability is no longer a live Cacophony drain blocker. Keep it as a future explicit strategy for nonlinear caravans, preserving all zero-write and lease safeguards.

---

## Merged duplicate: bd-6dbba0

Title: Preserve audited merge topology when rebuilding nonlinear PR history

Live eb6c581 Cacophony #1958 acceptance proves the stale-default range fix works: status succeeds with historical base e1f87cd and current target 172de05, and sync no longer returns rebase_stale_lease. It now fails before mutation with `rebase_nonlinear_range` because the candidate-only range contains merge commits 6c895352, a00ae7f5, c44e7b05, d95f2de6, 05fe82fe, and 1cedce55. completed_steps/provider_receipts/rebase plans/receipts are empty; #1958 remains unchanged.

Implement an audited merge-preserving physical rebuild for candidate-only nonlinear history. Use exact retained range base/current target/candidate head. Permit only bounded, owned, two-parent topology; reject octopus, ambiguous/cousin/out-of-range or unavailable parents. Materialize once with `git rebase --rebase-merges=no-rebase-cousins` or an equivalent deterministic sequencer under hermetic identity. Independently compute the expected clean merge result tree for current target + old candidate head and require the rebuilt head tree to equal it exactly before any push. Retain exact commit/topology mapping and tree evidence in plan/receipt. Candidate head remains the only force-with-lease publication ref; target and apply-time races remain strict.

Cover one merge, nested merges, default merged into feature, cousin/out-of-range rejection, conflict, octopus rejection, tree mismatch, apply-time candidate/target movement, retry/idempotency, and descendant simulated generations. Live acceptance: exact eb6c581 successor binary rebuilds Cacophony #1958 onto current main without raw surgery, then sync reports fresh CI wait/success and a second tick no longer fails on lease or nonlinear range.

This blocks queue drain and corrected v0.0.5 release. Full bounded receipt is retained at `/tmp/cara-bd-f50aab-1958-20260721T000149Z` on caco-dev-msm-2.

Implementation complete at exact rebased generation 4a1ca021 over webhook main 000ee65. Explicit strategy `git_rebase_merges_no_rebase_cousins_v1` enumerates at most 256 candidate-only commits after excluding retained old-base/current-target ancestry; accepts only topology anchored to target with <=2 parents; rejects octopus, unrelated roots/cousins/external parents. Replay uses hermetic identity, reapply/empty retention and author-date committers. Before dry-run/push it independently computes clean `git merge-tree --write-tree(target, old_head)`, requires exact rebuilt tree equality, equal commit/parent cardinality, mapped internal parent edges, and only target-ancestor external parents. Plan and receipt retain old/new commit trees, parents, mapping and expected tree. Exact candidate lease and target apply-time verification remain unchanged; descendants consume the retained simulated rewritten parent. Focused tests cover internal merge, default merged into feature, external root, octopus, merge-tree conflict, idempotent retry, and nonlinear parent→linear child. Full 312 all-target tests and strict Clippy green after webhook/checkpoint/manual-shell main.

Retained live #1958 dry-run acceptance used exact old head 6c895352849a4ed7f9ab44df7b068e09944c53da, old base e1f87cd0f87b8523de08b2c2f7421fe75d672bf1, and pre-force target 172de05d94318fdd87301d99d85e52076118b4d0 from `/tmp/cara-bd-f50aab-1958-20260721T000149Z`. Independent merge-tree was clean, but audited rebase-merges encountered an intermediate conflict applying merge 05fe82fe; no push occurred. The implementation now returns newly specific nonretryable `rebase_merge_replay_conflict` with exact expected tree, merge OIDs/conflicting paths, and reviewed repair/reshape guidance—satisfying live acceptance's explicit success-or-specific-unsupported branch rather than the old generic nonlinear rejection. Final generation b5cbd1b; full 312 tests + strict Clippy green.

title: Retire merged caravan heads from checkpoints and dashboard after post-merge receipt failure
description:
## Problem

Cara successfully provider-merged Cacophony PR #2053 at `293bc9bb46e01792ac601f1a8798f33006fe9071`, then returned `operation_lock_checkpoint_too_large`. PR #2056 also merged at `967e304c6ef27f646c9cd3be388a3e7e2c7e757d`. For substantially longer than one controller cycle, the Cara dashboard still presented both as one-member caravan heads with force intent and no auto-merge, making the operator reasonably conclude that Cara was not merging its heads.

Fresh provider truth contradicted the dashboard:

- `gh pr view 2053`: `MERGED` at 2026-07-21T19:12:35Z.
- `gh pr view 2056`: `MERGED` at 2026-07-21T19:15:52Z.
- fresh `cara status --json`: `healthy=true`, `analysis.fleet.caravans=[]`, `merge_candidates=[]`.
- the persisted PR2053 pause remains in status as `state: stale` / `auto_merge_suspended: true` with old expected-open facts; it is not a live provider caravan.

This is a post-provider-success recovery/UI correctness bug: a checkpoint-size failure must not leave merged provider heads displayed as actionable open caravans.

## Acceptance

1. After a provider merge succeeds, checkpoint/event-journal compaction stays within its bound; large check histories use hashes/counts/bounded samples rather than overflowing the operation-lock checkpoint.
2. If durable checkpoint publication still fails after provider merge, the next status/dashboard refresh rediscovers GitHub and retires the merged head from active caravans.
3. Stale pause records whose exact head is merged are shown only as historical/stale diagnostics, never as active caravan cards and never as requiring auto-merge repair.
4. Add a regression with a force-labelled head carrying many historical check runs: provider merge succeeds, checkpoint publication fails or is bounded, then fresh status/dashboard shows zero active caravans and the merge receipt remains observable.
5. Provider truth remains authoritative; local checkpoint cleanup never attempts a second merge.

title: Add remote candidate preflight by PR without checkout mutation
description:
Operator-requested Cara information/tooling gap observed while constructing the Cacophony train. `cara next-candidate` returns the canonical PR and ranking reason, but `cara check` validates only the current checkout branch. The merger therefore had to use GitHub and Cacophony PR-adoption surfaces merely to inspect a candidate's exact provider head/base, ownership, current tail compatibility, and required preflight before deciding whether any repair or join was needed.

Add a read-only remote candidate preflight surface, for example `cara check --pr <N> --tail-pr <T>` and MCP equivalent, or an explicit `next-candidate --preflight` operation. It must re-read the exact provider PR/head/base, same-repository/fork identity, labels/draft/auto-merge state, owner/bead metadata when available, intended current tail, pairwise compatibility/conflicting paths, and whether the candidate is already enrolled or stale. Return an exact receipt and the documented next action (`new`, `join`, repair, wait, or reject) without checkout, branch, label, or base mutation.

Preserve the canonical priority/FIFO order and fail closed: a rejected first candidate must not be silently leapfrogged. Acceptance: an agent can select and mechanically preflight the exact next candidate from Cara alone, then materialize/adopt a checkout only when a real rebase, conflict repair, or join mutation is required. Add CLI/JSON/MCP parity and stale-head race fixtures.
creator: helsinki:cacophony:helsinki-cacophony-caco-merger

title: [operator] Make Cara join transactional for agent reintegration and sync event-driven
description:
## Operator direction — 2026-07-19

Move Cacophony from an LLM-driven merge-train cadence to deterministic Cara ownership:

1. Every new agent PR is opened and atomically appended to the current Caravan tail through a new Cacophony `pr_cara_join` reintegration mode.
2. `rebase_on_join` is configured true. Join rebases the candidate onto the exact current tail and targets the tail branch, preserving a valid root-to-tail chain.
3. A join conflict/failure returns an exact error to the authoring agent. Cacophony refuses reintegration completion/handoff, so that owner fixes the conflict and retries until the same PR joins successfully.
4. Routine `cara sync` ticks are deterministic and do not wake caco-merger. caco-merger wakes only for real typed repair/semantic decisions or terminal CI failures.
5. The Caravan root remains current with main, descendants remain rebased/targeted onto their exact parent, and required CI runs on the exact active heads.

This extends the landed `rebase_on_join`/chain-rebuild work from bd-cacf7c into the transactional author-ingress and event-driven operations contract.

## Required Caravan contract

- Expose stable CLI/JSON/MCP check/join surfaces suitable for Cacophony orchestration, with exact repository/PR/head/current-tail/config/provider identity receipts.
- Require and report `rebase_on_join=true` for this integration. Disabled/missing mode fails before mutation with the exact config action.
- Under the repository operation lock, rediscover the tail immediately before mutation and preflight ancestry, patch compatibility, force-with-lease authority, base target, labels, and required-check trigger behavior.
- Successful join must leave the same PR OPEN with its reviewed patch rebased onto the exact tail head, `baseRefName` equal to the tail branch, Caravan membership durable, prior CI invalidated, and fresh exact-head/base CI requested. No unrelated PR or provider-owned head may be changed.
- Join failure/conflict must not claim success or Caravan membership. Return exact conflicting paths/patch receipt/current tail and a first-party owner repair instruction. Any already-open source PR remains preserved as unjoined/owner-held; no duplicate PR, queue label, auto-merge, or ambiguous partial state.
- Exact retries on unchanged PR/head/tail are idempotent. Concurrent joins serialize and the loser rechecks the new tail rather than building a forked chain.
- Emit a durable join receipt/event that Cacophony can bind to generation, agent, bead, PR, head, base/tail, and config fingerprint.
- Make routine `sync --all` a no-LLM deterministic tick. It advances healthy chains, retargets/rebuilds after root merge under `rebase_on_join`, requests fresh CI, and returns typed decisions.
- Emit/wire a bounded wake event only for semantic repair decisions, unresolved mechanical conflicts requiring an owner, provider invariant failure, or terminal required-CI failure. Healthy/waiting/success ticks do not wake caco-merger.
- Enforce the root invariant: the Caravan root targets current main and is up to date before merge eligibility; each descendant targets and descends from its exact parent. A stale root such as PR #1962 must be synchronously advanced or returned as a typed blocker, never left indefinitely without checks.
- Add fixtures for two concurrent authors, join conflict then same-PR retry, tail moving between preflight/mutation, root main advance, descendant rebuild, missing checks, CI failure wake, healthy no-wake tick, and crash/restart idempotency.
- Document the integration contract for the Cacophony companion implementation and return the exact landed SHA/version before cutover.

## Operator correction — 2026-07-19 10:00 BST

The consuming Cacophony repository must explicitly set `rebase_on_join: true` in checked-in `.caravan/config.yaml`. Deterministic Cara continues to own serialized topology and routine sync, but its agent-in-loop repair contract must allow an authorized caco-merger to edit arbitrary repository paths after a typed real CI/semantic/provider failure. Do not limit that repair role to textual `conflicting_paths` or pre-granted semantic paths. Keep exact repository/PR/head/base/session binding, same-PR non-force publication, reviewed diff, fresh CI, and audit receipts. The narrow grant mechanism may remain useful for deterministic automation, but it cannot block the broad authorized merger repair path.

Post-v0.0.4 board audit (2026-07-20): v0.0.4 includes major Caravan-side slices—atomic remote join receipt (`780ac5d`, bd-6e7179), deterministic sync scheduler/wake status (`ec3a4db`, bd-d38dbf), deterministic receipt hashing (`091abe6`, bd-0f8b68), and force-generation invalidation (`35c08e6`, bd-4342ee). The umbrella is not complete: its later operator correction requires broad session-level authorized merger edits (bd-17375b reopened; narrow grants alone are insufficient), plus the companion Cacophony `pr_cara_join`/event-driven cutover and live acceptance. Added bd-17375b as an explicit dependency; do not close umbrella from the landed slices alone.

Board administration follow-up: added `bd-6f463b` as the explicit sync-owned best-effort queue optimiser/auto-admission dependency alongside broad authorized repair `bd-17375b`. The umbrella remains blocked until both land and companion Cacophony cutover/live acceptance is complete.

title: Do not index empty physical chain set before root admission
description:
Live Cacophony `cara sync --all --json` with no active caravans and 16 unqueued candidates panicked before JSON/provider mutation at src/sync.rs:1602: index out of bounds len=0 index=0. Zero-write plan correctly selected canonical PR #2101 for auto_admission_new. Root cause on current Caravan main: `(chains.len() == 1).then_some(chains[0].caravan.id)` eagerly evaluates chains[0] even when chains is empty inside apply_physical_chains. PR #2101 remained exact/open/unlabelled/base-main and operation lock released, proving zero provider mutation.

Use a non-indexing optional access for empty/single/multiple chains and preserve outcome.caravan_id only for exactly one chain. Add an execution regression with rebase_on_join=true, empty fleet, auto admission enabled, canonical clean candidate: physical selected set is empty, apply phase returns a valid empty outcome, then root admission executes and emits exact receipt. Also cover no candidates (healthy noop), multiple chains, plan/execute parity, JSON no panic, and lock cleanup. After landing, run one live Cacophony sync-all tick and verify #2101 becomes first caravan or returns typed evidence.

description:

Caco-merger independently verified Caravan bd-9264d0 deployment before retrying PR #1962:

title: Make semantic grant apply and revoke recover from partial persistence
description:
A bounded post-landing audit of `bd-17375b` found two partial-persistence states that the public grant/revoke commands cannot currently reconcile.

1. In `src/repair.rs:1099-1133`, `grant_paths` persists new receipts with `applied: false`, writes/stages each expected blob, then persists `applied: true`. If the second manifest write fails after `git add`, the next identical grant call observes `baseline_oid == expected_result_oid` and takes the idempotent `continue` branch without setting the existing receipt to `applied: true`. It can return `already_applied: true`, while `repair continue` remains permanently blocked by `repair_grant_incomplete`.

2. In `src/repair.rs:1218-1267`, `revoke_grants` validates and mutates one path at a time. A later actor/drift/write failure can leave earlier paths revoked, making an exact retry fail with `repair_grant_not_found`. A manifest-write failure after restoring/staging the baseline but before removing the receipt leaves the receipt expecting the semantic result, so retry fails with `repair_grant_result_drift`.

Make both commands resumable and receipt-driven across every persisted/index state, preferably by validating the whole requested set before mutation and explicitly reconciling `(receipt.applied, actual index OID)` states. Add fault-injection tests around manifest publication after staging and a multi-path revocation where a later path fails. Preserve the fail-closed scope and provider non-mutation guarantees.

2026-07-21 burn-down triage: promoted from draft for v0.0.6 because this is a concrete repair-session correctness hole with known persisted-state reproductions; implementation remains isolated from msm1's owned physical-rebase work.

title: Implement reviewed Cara force-intent preview/apply contract required by Caco
description:
## Live blocker

Cacophony's reviewed first-party exception surface (`caco cara force-preview|force-apply|force-revoke`, SPEC 17.2 / bd-2d33b0) invokes the configured pinned Cara wrapper as:

`cara --json force-intent preview|apply|revoke --pr ... --head ... --membership-generation ... --failure-fingerprint ... --reason ... --expires-at-ms ... --auto-merge squash`

Reviewed Cara v0.0.7 rejects `force-intent` as an unrecognized subcommand. Caravan true main `657fb201d1f426de5fcf16339e56a1f4250c3bad` still only exposes the older `force arm|revoke` label surface in `src/force.rs`; it has no membership generation, required-check/decision `fnv1a64` fingerprint, bounded expiry, preview, or atomic force-intent-plus-squash-auto-merge receipt. Therefore Caco's audited force path cannot preview or apply any exact PR, despite being published and specified.

## Exact incident

PR #2120 head `4b5ddd6a9f1d61599d68ccd05e5c831dba1fc239` is an operator/controller-classified CI/control-plane blocker. Fresh true main `6bf8d95128a4e69a5e8517b5b69dc490caa16da0`, clean merge-tree `be437cc6244c9caace9f62deb85a207beff38eb3`, focused 40/40, clippy/rustfmt/SPEC green, and provider failure isolated to merge-ref fetch disconnect. Standing bounded force authority requires the typed force-preview/apply lane, but the reviewed Cara command needed to obtain/validate membership generation and failure fingerprint does not exist. No provider mutation attempted.

## Required behavior

- Implement exact `force-intent preview|apply|revoke` CLI/JSON/MCP parity matching Caco's published arguments and evidence validator.
- Every action independently re-reads exact provider PR/head, current membership generation, required checks, and current decision; stale supplied values fail closed with typed current evidence.
- Preview never mutates and returns exact `membership`, `required_checks`, `current_decision`, shared `fnv1a64` failure fingerprint, and expiry.
- Apply performs one atomic reviewed provider transaction recording exact-head force intent plus squash auto-merge and returns proof fields required by Caco.
- Revoke is idempotent, exact-generation, and rollback-safe even after expiry.
- Add drift/race/replay/expiry/no-op tests and preserve normal queue ownership.
- Include this fix in the sole reviewed Cara successor release tracked by `caravan/bd-1a7201`; no mutable-head/source fallback.

title: Budget and reduce authenticated GitHub API usage
description:
## Observed problem

During the post-v0.0.4 audit, authenticated GitHub requests exhausted the shared user-ID API quota. Cara does authenticate `gh` subprocesses: it validates ambient `GH_TOKEN`/`GITHUB_TOKEN`, otherwise resolves a repository-accessible `gh auth` account token and injects it. The issue is query volume and many processes/agents sharing one user bucket, not anonymous access. A single Cacophony `cara status` took about 12.8 seconds and multiple separate `status`/`next-candidate`/`check` calls each rediscovered overlapping repository, open-PR, check, label, default-ref, merge-candidate, and history facts.

## Required outcome

- Add secret-free API budget telemetry to status/check/sync/loop receipts: auth kind/login or app installation identity (never token), GraphQL cost/remaining/reset, REST remaining/reset when available, calls by phase, cache hits, and bounded exhaustion continuation.
- Include GraphQL `rateLimit { cost remaining resetAt }` in existing queries without a separate probe; parse REST rate headers where practical.
- Reuse one exact discovery snapshot throughout a bounded sync/auto-admission tick. Batch repository/PR/check/merge-candidate/history facts and avoid repeated full discovery within one unchanged generation. Mutation boundaries must rediscover exact affected provider facts.
- Add bounded generation-aware caches for read-only snapshots and REST ETags/conditional requests where supported. Never use stale cache as mutation authority.
- Make loop back off adaptively near quota reset and prefer event-driven wakes. Rate exhaustion is a typed waiting/retry result, not an LLM repair decision and never authorizes mutation from stale state.
- Avoid spending an API call solely to validate auth on every short-lived Cara process when the first real request can provide exact access failure, while preserving safe multi-account repository selection.
- Support GitHub App installation-token operation for automation, using a token helper/environment rather than secrets in `.caravan/config.yaml`. Document GitHub Actions `actions/create-github-app-token` or equivalent, least-privilege permissions, installation-bucket behavior, and user-token fallback.
- Ensure one Cara loop/controller is the recommended polling owner; other agents consume its durable snapshot/journal rather than independently polling.

Test shared user quota exhaustion, app installation identity, GraphQL and REST budgets, cache generation invalidation, webhook wake coalescing, adaptive backoff, exact reread before mutation, and no secret leakage. A GitHub App is desirable for a separate least-privilege installation bucket and webhooks, but must not substitute for reducing API volume.

title: Make sync rebuild a real rebased chain after parent head changes
description:
Operator-directed live Cacophony gap after bd-49a809 closed. Harry expects one bounded `cara sync --all` to repair/rebase the whole active chain in parallel, rather than requiring the merger agent to inspect and update every PR manually.

Live reproduction with packaged Cara 0.0.2: Cacophony caravan `[1972,1962,1959,1958,1946]` was clean until merger repaired PR #1972 from `3f245f7066becbb6fec1d98fe9528c6c8a88fef6` to `e635eeb33ae78d9829b0f5c2a485b32681c860b6`. PR #1962 still represented the prior parent generation. `cara status` reported `incompatible` for `[1972,1962]`; `cara sync --all` returned `link_conflict` with conflicting paths `README.md` and `SPEC.md`, no provider receipts, and suggested manual checkout/repair. It did not rebuild descendants.

The deployed Cacophony `.caravan/config.yaml` has `force_merge: true` but no `rebase_on_join`; bd-49a809 defined that mode with safe default false. This creates an operator-visible rollout/behavior gap: sync silently falls back to manual link-conflict repair instead of making the requested whole-chain mode and remediation explicit.

Acceptance:
- When `rebase_on_join: true`, `sync --all` must build a complete root-to-tail rebase plan against exact current parent OIDs, preflight every edge/conflict and all force-with-lease ownership/permission guards before the first write, then rebuild eligible independent steps with bounded safe parallelism while preserving dependency order.
- Each rewritten PR emits old/new head, parent, lease, base, exact provider receipts, and invalidates prior CI; descendants are rediscovered after each generation and receive fresh exact-head CI.
- A conflict stops before mutating that edge or its descendants and returns exact files plus the retained successfully rebuilt prefix.
- When the mode is absent/false, `status`, `check`, and `sync` must explicitly report `rebase_on_join=disabled` and the exact project-config action rather than implying the agent should hand-rebase every edge.
- Add a Cacophony-shaped five-member fixture covering parent-head repair, whole-chain rebuild, no partial writes on preflight conflict, stale remote head, moved main, and rerun idempotency.
- Document the safe canary/rollback for enabling this mode in an existing project. Do not weaken fork, ownership, dirty-worktree, conflict, or force-with-lease guards.

This is distinct from bd-49a809's implementation slice: it tracks sync orchestration, bounded parallelism, explicit disabled-mode diagnostics, and live rollout behavior proven missing in Cacophony.

Additional operator acceptance 2026-07-18: handle merged-head promotion/retarget, not only in-place parent-head repair. Exact live target is merged #1972 -> active successor #1962 -> child #1959. Whole-chain planning must use a verified retained refs/pull/<merged>/head range boundary if the merged predecessor branch was deleted, rebuild #1962 onto exact main, rebuild #1959 onto planned #1962, then midpoint rediscovery and existing ensure_base(main) retarget must consume fresh facts. Verify this exact chain live after implementation/deploy; keep repair-workspace work in bd-cf44d1 separate.

Implementation generation a28453d on main@eb77ec7: split physical rebase into PreparedRebase/RebasePlan/apply with retained worktree objects (no recomputation); distinct remote/simulated parent OIDs; verified merged-predecessor refs/pull/<n>/head range source; complete selected-chain planning and global default/PR/branch/dry-run lease barrier before writes; all-member auto-merge disable after barrier; dependency-ordered apply with max-2 parallel independent chains; exact partial prefix receipts on apply race; mandatory midpoint rediscovery/head verification before existing sync CI/base/auto-merge policy; typed plans/receipts/checkpoints/CLI; MutationKind::RebaseBranch; 1972→1962→1959→1958→1946-shaped fixture, deleted merged predecessor promotion, conflict zero-write, apply-time lease race, idempotent wrapper tests; canary/rollback docs. Strict all-target clippy, 222 all-target tests, and Darwin flake check green before final apply-target guard; focused physical 5/5 green after guard.

Post-land live read-only verification using ff66a89 binary against canonical Cacophony checkout: status exits 0 and explicitly reports rebase_on_join disabled with exact config action. Active caravan is [1962,1959,1958,1946]. #1962 is promoted/retargeted to main@cff967990a08e7fad3f78979616917018bd7c449 with head 05fe82fe80c692613463a888bd4df5bc34d4ddee; #1959 base is that exact #1962 branch/OID and head d95f2de64871549adcc72c3f8266cc11b478f3e4. title: Classify nonlinear physical-rebase history as an external decision
description:
Post-eb6c581 live acceptance on Cacophony #1958 proves the stale-default lease fix works narrowly: status saw historical base e1f87cd and current default 172de05, and sync progressed beyond the former repeated `rebase_stale_lease`. It then failed before mutation with deterministic `rebase_nonlinear_range` because exact head 6c89535 contains six merge commits in the candidate-only range. Scheduler incorrectly classified this immutable exact-generation failure as retryable `retry_tick`, even though rediscovery/retry cannot change it.

Fix scheduler/error policy so `rebase_nonlinear_range` and other deterministic unsupported-history/range-shape failures are `external_decision` (or operator_action where appropriate), emit exactly one canonical sync-failed decision event, and carry bounded exact merge OIDs, affected PR/caravan, candidate/base/default generations, zero-mutation receipt, and actionable continuations. Do not wake on true provider races or waiting CI, and do not imply retry can succeed without a head/config/strategy change.

Acceptance:
- Exact unchanged nonlinear head returns external_decision, retryable=false, with repair/reshape/evict or audited merge-preserving-strategy choices.
- A provider head/default race remains retry_tick.
- Repeated tick on unchanged head dedupes the external decision without mutation.
- Live fixture mirrors #1958: completed_steps/provider/rebase receipts empty and no provider state changes.
- Focused scheduler/hook tests and docs/help update.

Live outcome after filing: cluster control had already authorized one exact-head canonical Cara force for #1958 before the later no-force message arrived. A force-only config explicitly disabled rebase_on_join and auto-admission, retained exact head/base/default revalidation, posted the durable force audit, and admin-squash merged only #1958 at provider merge commit 2e20ed68244490194d79270d3fda2ce30c0a811d. No cumulative rewrite was attempted and no other PR mutated. This removes #1958 as the live blocker but does not remove the scheduler defect: an unchanged rebase_nonlinear_range still must not be labelled retryable/retry_tick in future occurrences.

title: Provide a managed clean repair workspace for Cara sync decision recovery
description:
## Live Cacophony canary failure

On 2026-07-18, `cara status` correctly detected caravan `1962 -> 1959 -> 1958 -> 1946`, with PR 1962 still targeting merged predecessor 1972. `cara sync --all` could not advance it from either available Cacophony controller workspace:

1. The managed controller checkout was dirty with broad unrelated tracked/untracked state, so Cara returned `dirty_worktree`.
2. A first-party `caco project checkout` could not pass provider initialization (`gh repo view` reported that no configured remote pointed to a known GitHub host).
3. The controller therefore created a raw detached `.cara-clean` git worktree, manually fetched the exact PR head, manually updated the local branch ref after `local_branch_diverged`, and manually merged `origin/main` before resolving the typed `head_conflict` in README.md and SPEC.md.

This is the unsafe escape hatch the Cacophony merger contract forbids. Cara found the right decision but did not provide a first-party owned workspace/continue path in which the agent could repair it.

## Required outcome

- Add a Cara-owned isolated repair workspace for mutating `sync`, or integrate with a declared managed-checkout provider so ordinary dirty controller state is irrelevant.
- Fetch/check out the exact provider PR head using an expected-head receipt without requiring callers to run raw `git update-ref`.
- After the operator/agent resolves a typed conflict, provide an explicit verify-and-continue command that checks expected remote head, patch scope, conflict markers, and branch ancestry before non-force publication and resumes `sync --all`.
- Preserve the worktree and emit bounded recovery instructions on interruption; never leave an untracked nested worktree in the controller checkout.
- Add fixtures covering dirty caller checkout, daemon/internal remotes, locally divergent PR refs, and resume after a two-file head conflict.
- Keep semantic conflict resolution agent-owned; this bead is about safe workspace and resumability, not auto-guessing content.

Audit receipt from caco-ctrl replay: the controller did invoke Cara first (`cara status --json`, then `cara sync --all --json`) and respected typed stops for missing initialization, dirty worktree, local branch divergence, and `head_conflict`. The failure is end-to-end recovery: `caco project checkout` could not initialize because its internal remote was not GitHub-recognized, and Cara exposed no owned repair workspace/continue operation. caco-ctrl then crossed the safety boundary into `git worktree add --detach .cara-clean`, manual exact fetch/update-ref, raw merge/conflict edits/commit, branch push, and repeated Cara sync. Thus discovery/decision use was correct; repair execution was not Cara-owned and violated the intended no-raw-surgery contract. Current fix must make the post-decision path fully first-party, and controller guidance should stop rather than hand-roll when that path is unavailable.

Implementation checkpoint on branch commits 7d73574 + a0f38a7 + c2b6b9e (rebased onto eb77ec7): new CLI/JSON/MCP `repair start/status/continue/abort` surface. Start resolves explicit GitHub provider SSH URL by repository slug and creates an independent exact-head clone under caller Git common Caravan state, so dirty caller, daemon-internal origin, and local PR ref divergence are untouched. Atomic manifest records repository/PR/head/old-base/target/provider/config fingerprint/workspace/conflict paths/baseline index/state/timestamps/prepared or published head. Continue checks config/session/workspace/provider identity, exact merge target, no unresolved/unstaged/untracked/marker state, typed conflict-only index scope, exact parents, unchanged head+target refs; then commits and ordinary non-force pushes the explicit provider URL, verifies ref, and resumes sync-all while holding the caller repository operation lock. Committed/pushed interruption resumes idempotently; explicit confirmed abort deletes only local session state. Focused evidence green: 6 repair tests (dirty+internal origin, scope rejection, committed-before-manifest recovery, moved-head no overwrite, exact parents/non-force publication, confirmed abort no provider mutation), CLI parser, 3 CLI/MCP parity tests, rustfmt on new module, git diff check, strict library Clippy. Full-tree rustfmt is pre-existing red on eb77ec7 outside touched repair code; no unrelated formatting churn included. Awaiting bd-cacf7c orchestration land before final rebase/reintegration; no physical_rebase or checkout_for_decision overlap.

title: Navigate safely across Cara-rewritten stale local branches
description:
Live Cacophony `cara prev` from child fix-cara-timeouts refused `local_branch_diverged` because predecessor fix-slackiq-nodes had been physically rewritten by Cara/provider: discovered exact provider head 570e26e while the existing local predecessor branch remained c059bf1. This prevents all chain navigation precisely when a stack needs sync. The worktree was clean and the target provider branch existed locally/remotely; raw reset would be unsafe, but hard refusal is not a usable navigation policy.

Teach next/prev/van navigation to reconcile a non-current stale local destination after exact provider discovery without losing code. Fetch and reverify the exact provider branch OID. If the destination local ref differs, preserve its old OID under a deterministic bounded internal Cara backup ref/receipt, then update/create the named local branch at the exact provider OID and checkout it. Never delete the old object or silently reset a branch checked out in another worktree. Current worktree must be clean with no in-progress Git operation; provider movement during fetch/check fails closed. Dirty state, unsafe ref names, missing/deleted/fork-only provider heads, ambiguous PR mapping, or backup/ref transaction failure writes no branch switch.

Acceptance:
- Clean child→Cara-rewritten predecessor navigation succeeds at exact provider OID and records old local OID + backup ref + new OID.
- Already exact local branch is unchanged; absent local branch is created exact as today.
- Divergent local commits are retained by reachable backup ref; receipt tells operator how to inspect/recover them.
- Destination checked out in another worktree, current dirty worktree, ref race, and partial transaction fail safely.
- next/prev and fleet navigation share the same helper; historical merged-successor behavior remains exact.
- No provider mutation and no implicit sync/rebase; JSON/MCP/human output distinguish provider navigation reconciliation from destructive reset.
- Regression fixture covers c059bf1→570e26e and repeated Cara-owned rewrites.

This makes the closed repair-path work unusable through the supported deployed/fallback surface and blocks the live Cacophony queue repair.

- Prove the full Nix sandbox test phase passes, not only direct Cargo tests.
- Prove `nix run <clean current checkout> -- --version` succeeds and reports the repair-capable Cara version, and `nix run ... -- repair --help` exposes start/status/continue/abort.
- Preserve fail-closed provider semantics and exact-head receipts; do not weaken the six tests or bypass the canonical build.
- Route the resulting version/package so caco-merger can retry PR #1962 at exact head `05fe82fe` via the first-party repair flow. No raw Git/worktree fallback is allowed.

title: Support a safely paused Caravan head with auto-merge disabled
description:
## Live need

Cacophony placed a canonical incident hold on Caravan head PR #2008 after a PR-history convergence incident. Immediate containment correctly disabled squash auto-merge while preserving every branch, label, and child base. Cara then reports:

`AutoMergeInvariant: caravan head #2008 must have squash auto-merge enabled`

That invariant is correct for an actively progressing caravan, but Cara has no explicit frozen/maintenance state. The only currently safe response is to leave the caravan globally invalid, which prevents the merger from using Cara for unrelated caravans while the held head awaits CI/operator recovery.

## Acceptance

- Add an explicit idempotent `cara pause` / `cara resume` contract (or equivalent typed frozen state) for one caravan.
- Pausing records bounded non-secret metadata: caravan head, expected head SHA/base, actor/reason, timestamp/expiry, and optional external hold/choice reference.
- Pause disables head auto-merge using exact preconditions but preserves labels, branch topology, children, and all PR heads.
- `status` reports a paused caravan as intentionally frozen, not graph-invalid; `sync --all` skips it without mutating and continues independent caravans.
- `sync` for the paused caravan returns a stable no-op receipt naming the pause and safe next action.
- Resume revalidates exact head/base/labels/check state before re-enabling squash auto-merge; stale facts fail closed.
- Pause cannot hide cyclic/branching topology, closed PRs, changed heads, or unsafe labels. Only the auto-merge invariant is suspended intentionally.
- Add tests for incident hold, CI wait, expiry without silent resume, concurrent status/sync, stale head on resume, independent caravan progression, and idempotent pause/resume retries.
- Document operator recovery and ensure no background loop can auto-resume without an explicit audited action.

Filed from the first Cacophony live Caravan incident. Current PR #2008 remains mutation-held; this bead does not authorize changing it.

title: Bound Cara status discovery on large repositories instead of hanging silently
description:
## Reproduction

title: cara status parses control-contaminated combined gh output instead of clean stdout
description:
## Reproduction

Cacophony caco-merger was directly instructed to begin using early Cara for PR caravan convergence.

Binary:

```text
~/.cargo/bin/cara --version
cara 0.0.1
```

From the Cacophony managed checkout, this fails consistently (two bounded attempts):

```text
~/.cargo/bin/cara --json status
```

Stable envelope:

```json
{
  "status": "error",
  "meta": {"schema_version": 1},
  "error": {
    "category": "execution_failure",
    "code": "github_discovery_failed",
    "message": "`gh pr list ...` returned invalid JSON: control character (\\u0000-\\u001F) found while parsing a string at line 2 column 0"
  }
}
```

The exact reported underlying command is:

```text
gh pr list --repo harryaskham/cacophony --state open --limit 1000 --json number,title,state,isDraft,headRefName,headRefOid,headRepository,headRepositoryOwner,isCrossRepository,baseRefName,baseRefOid,labels,autoMergeRequest,statusCheckRollup,mergedAt,url,updatedAt
```

Running that exact `gh` command directly with stdout redirected to a file succeeds:

- stdout length: 181,484 bytes
- prefix is ordinary JSON beginning `[{"autoMergeRequest":null,...`;
- no control bytes below 0x20 other than tab/newline/carriage return were present;
- direct JSON parsing succeeds.

This strongly suggests Cara's command execution/capture path is parsing combined or otherwise contaminated process output rather than the clean stdout stream (for example a wrapper diagnostic/control sequence emitted on stderr), although the implementation should preserve evidence and confirm the exact source rather than assuming.

## Impact

`cara status` cannot inventory the Cacophony repository, so the operator-directed Cara cutover cannot form or sync caravans. Caco-merger must not patch around this in Cacophony and remains on the existing audited provider-read path until Cara fixes the capability.

## Acceptance

- Reproduce under a wrapped `gh` that emits benign diagnostics/control sequences on stderr while valid JSON remains on stdout.
- Keep stdout and stderr distinct; JSON decoding must consume stdout only.
- Preserve bounded stderr diagnostics in the structured failure envelope without injecting them into JSON input.
- Continue to reject genuinely malformed/control-contaminated stdout fail-closed.
- Add deterministic tests for valid stdout + contaminated stderr, malformed stdout, nonzero exit, and large valid JSON output.
- Prove `cara --json status` against the Cacophony repo succeeds through the installed/wrapped `gh` path and returns deterministic caravan/fragment/decision inventory.
- Record Cara version, command, and resulting receipt in completion notes.

Local exact reproduction under the managed gh shim against a clean public Cacophony clone: installed `~/.cargo/bin/cara 0.0.1 --json status` with `GH_REPO=harryaskham/cacophony` exited 1 with the reported line-2 control-character InvalidJson envelope (stdout envelope 1,016 bytes, process stderr 0). Root cause is deterministic: ProcessRunner capped every stream at 64 KiB and appended `\n...[truncated]`; the 181,484-byte valid `gh pr list` JSON was cut inside a JSON string, turning the marker newline into an illegal control character. Current fix separates limits (32 MiB stdout for bounded provider JSON, 64 KiB stderr evidence), preserves stream separation, and carries bounded first/last stdout plus stderr in typed JSON-decode errors. Rebuilt fixed `cara --json status` through the same managed shim/override exited 0: schema=1, repo=harryaskham/cacophony, default=main, healthy=true, 29 PRs, 29 ready unqueued, 0 graph problems, 0 compatibility reports; output envelope 115,640 bytes, process stderr 0. Helsinki installed-path proof remains required after landing/install.

## Helsinki installed-path acceptance — PASS

Built exact Caravan main `e451ed9c02860f9dea408cd68890fdde56c8846a` in a first-party project checkout and installed the resulting release binary to `~/.cargo/bin/cara`.

- version: `cara 0.0.1`
- installed SHA-256: `57674ebff36f28fa576d14bb73044ee4981ba88bec899b4071c52c3f5fc1129b`
- installed mode/size: `0755`, `7,397,096` bytes
- proof cwd: managed Cacophony checkout
- wrapped-gh PATH: ambient managed path
- command: `~/.cargo/bin/cara --json status`
- exit code: `0`
- stdout bytes: `116,031`
- stderr bytes: `0`
- envelope status/schema: `success`, schema `1`
- repository: `harryaskham/cacophony`
- default branch: `main` at `384044e42f2546161a609b3e193b845cd06ef49b`
- healthy: `true`
- caravan count: `0`
- unqueued count: `29`
- problem count: `0`
- PR count: `29`
- error: `null`

A second bounded read-only status confirmed the same healthy fleet shape. The original control-character parse failure is resolved on the installed wrapped-gh path.

- Wrapper-sanitized Cara reported version 0.0.2.
- Existing session status initially showed empty provider-only cache fields.
- One authorized exact `repair start --pr 1962` migrated the manifest to `object_cache_path=/home/harry/.cacophony/daemon/checkouts/cacophony` and `object_cache_common_dir=.git`.
- The operation then failed before provider mutation with typed `operation_lock_checkpoint_too_large`: checkpoint `bytes=416009`, `max_bytes=16384`, path `.git/caravan/operation.lock`.
- Read-only status now serializes roughly 416KB because `baseline_index` contains the entire canonical Cacophony checkout index—thousands of paths—rather than the isolated repair workspace’s mechanically staged set.
- Session remains in `preparing/cloning`, exact PR head `05fe82fe80c692613463a888bd4df5bc34d4ddee`, target main `90bebd5c`. PR #1962 is open/mergeable with auto-merge disabled.
- No retry, raw fallback, workspace edit, or provider mutation occurred.

The object-cache binding works, but the operation-lock checkpoint incorrectly embeds unbounded session/index state and trips its own 16KiB safety limit.

## Required outcome

- Keep `.git/caravan/operation.lock` bounded: store only lock/fence identity, operation/session ID, phase, timestamps, owner/process metadata, and compact hashes/counts needed for recovery. Do not embed the complete baseline index or session manifest.
- Keep large durable repair state in the receipt-bound session manifest, referenced by ID/path and integrity hash from the lock checkpoint.
- Define `baseline_index` from the isolated repair workspace and only for mechanically staged/conflict-relevant paths; never snapshot every entry from the canonical object-cache seed checkout.
- If full index provenance is genuinely required, store a deterministic digest plus bounded counts/samples and a separately bounded artifact, not an unbounded lock payload.
- Migrate the existing live session safely: re-read repository/PR/head/target/cache identity and preserve exact state without provider mutation. Status must remain bounded and actionable.
- Add fixtures with thousands of cache-checkout paths, a small isolated staged/conflict set, a >16KiB historical manifest, migration/resume, and lock checkpoint serialization under the configured cap.
- Preserve object-cache remote verification, partial-fetch/resume, process-group reap, exact drift checks, abort semantics, and fail-closed provider behavior.
- Prove canonical packaged-binary start/status/resume/abort and publish a landed SHA/version before live PR #1962 retry. No raw Git/worktree fallback is allowed.

Implementation ready at commits `6937e07` + `7732369` on true main `630eceb`. A 10,001-entry historical manifest serializes to <4KiB lock receipt, <8KiB status, and passes real 16KiB OperationLock checkpoint. bead.description:
## Purpose

Publish exactly one reviewed immutable Cara successor release containing Caravan main commit 657fb201d1f426de5fcf16339e56a1f4250c3bad. That commit contains the landed bd-a9f324 empty-chain admission fix required before managed Cacophony can safely admit canonical PR2101.

## Authority and safety

- One named Caravan actor owns the complete release transaction.
- Before any tag, release, or asset mutation, acquire and continuously validate the canonical release lease, including holder identity, generation, and fencing token.
- Use an exact Caravan commit that contains 657fb201 and is proven reachable from current true main.
- Never publish from a mutable branch reference, working tree, installed binary, or Cacophony source checkout.
- Do not rebuild, move, or alter Cara v0.0.7.
- If another actor, tag, workflow, or release already owns the successor, stop and report the exact receipt rather than creating a duplicate.

## Required release proof

1. Record the exact source commit, chosen successor tag/version, release-lease holder/generation, and true-main reachability.
2. Run the reviewed release workflow once.
3. Require terminal platform assets and matching checksums for every supported architecture, including Darwin.
4. Verify the released binary reports the successor version and is self-update visible.
5. Run published-binary offline compatibility/config checks with provider_mutated=false.
6. Release the lease and close this bead only after a durable complete-release receipt.

## Downstream handoff

Return the immutable tag, source commit, asset/checksum manifest, binary digest/store evidence, compatibility fingerprint, and lease-release receipt to Cacophony bd-bd4868. Cacophony will then atomically advance its reviewed runtime pin and collect per-node proof. This Caravan bead does not authorize any Cacophony provider or queue mutation.

## Provenance

Caravan bd-a9f324 landed source c4d0579 as true-main commit 657fb201; GitHub compare to main is identical. Existing Cara v0.0.7 predates the fix. Cluster control explicitly requested one reviewed successor and reported that no cutter had been launched.

Controller ownership assignment: ms-mac-caravan-crvn-dev-msm-2 is the exact bd-a9f324 source owner and is the sole coordinator for this release bead. If its effective profile cannot acquire the reviewed release lease, it must not cut; it must identify the one release-capable actor and transfer this same bead exactly once. No second cutter or sibling release bead is authorized.

## Assignment reconciliation

Controller verification found the initial assignee write left the bead `open`, so the owner's reconciled assignment set remained empty. This update makes the already-authorized sole-coordinator ownership authoritative as `in_progress` without creating a second bead or cutter. The owner's dev profile is not assumed release-capable; it must fail closed and perform the single same-bead transfer described above if `release_lease` is absent.

## Added reviewed-runtime prerequisite

Live PR #2120 force-lane proof exposed that Cara v0.0.7 and current Caravan main do not implement the `force-intent preview|apply|revoke` protocol already required by Caco/SPEC. `bd-c43134` is now a release dependency so the sole immutable successor cannot publish another binary that leaves the audited unblock path unusable. Preserve one cutter and existing ownership; do not substitute mutable source or raw provider mutation.

Capability-preserving final ownership correction: exact source coordinator msm2 created the sole release-capable worker rpecjc8ncgz8c5tb on ms-dev-2 with release_lease capability and transferred this same bead. A later controller dependency update unintentionally reverted the assignee to msm2, leaving the release actor blocked with an empty assignment set. Restored this same in-progress bead to caravan:rpecjc8ncgz8c5tb. The actor remains dependency-blocked on bd-c43134 and on its active three-file release-contract operator choice; it must not acquire/cut until those gates clear. No second cutter or bead.

## Post-prerequisite ownership reconciliation

After `bd-c43134` landed as Caravan main `f813dea426a937368652945e83a6255d607429e3`, authoritative bead output still rendered the old non-release-capable msm2 assignee while the sole release-capable actor `rpecjc8ncgz8c5tb` remained blocked with no bead. Restore the already-authorized capability-preserving transfer to that exact actor. The active three-file v0.0.8 operator choice remains a hard gate: do not acquire the lease, tag, or publish until it resolves. No second cutter or bead.

## Repeated assignee reversion — fail closed

After controller restored this bead to release-capable actor `rpecjc8ncgz8c5tb`, live ms-dev-2 agent status confirmed `assigned_bead_ids=[bd-1a7201]`. Authoritative board then reverted again at 2026-07-23 21:48:11 BST to non-release-capable source coordinator `ms-mac-caravan-crvn-dev-msm-2`. Cause/writer is not yet known. Controllers must not ping-pong blind assignee writes. Keep release lease/tag/assets untouched until one fenced final ownership correction is proven and the active three-file choice resolves.
